courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20C or MATH 31BH and MATH 18 or MATH 31AH with a grade of C– or better. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Vector Calculus
courses.description: Change of variable in multiple integrals, Jacobian, Line integrals, Green’s theorem. Vector fields, gradient fields, divergence, curl. Spherical/cylindrical coordinates. Taylor series in several variables. Surface integrals, Stoke’s theorem. Gauss’ theorem. Conservative fields.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 20F or MATH 31AH and MATH 20C (or MATH 21C) or MATH 31BH with a grade of C– or better.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Honors Linear Algebra
courses.description: First quarter of a very rigorous three-quarter honors integrated linear algebra/multivariable calculus sequence for extremely well-prepared students. Topics include real/complex number systems, vector spaces, linear transformations, bases and dimension, change of basis, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, diagonalization. (Credit not offered for both MATH 31AH and 18.)
courses.prerequisites_text: AP Calculus BC score of 5. Students without an AP Math BC score of 5 may enroll with a prerequisite of MATH 20A-B with a grade of A or better in each. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: First-year Student Seminar
courses.description: The First-year Student Seminar Program is designed to provide new students with the opportunity to explore an intellectual topic with a faculty member in a small seminar setting. First-year student seminars are offered in all campus departments and undergraduate colleges, and topics vary from quarter to quarter. Enrollment is limited to fifteen to twenty students, with preference given to entering first-year students.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Putnam Seminar
courses.description: Students will develop skills in analytical thinking as they solve and present solutions to challenging mathematical problems in preparation for the William Lowell Putnam Mathematics Competition, a national undergraduate mathematics examination held each year. Students must sit for at least one half of the Putnam exam (given the first Saturday in December) to receive a passing grade. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit up to four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: AP Calculus AB score of 4 or more, or AP Calculus BC score of 3 or more, or MATH 20A.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Abstract Algebra I
courses.description: First course in a rigorous three-quarter introduction to the methods and basic structures of higher algebra. Topics include groups, subgroups and factor groups, homomorphisms, rings, fields. (Students may not receive credit for both MATH 100A and MATH 103A.)
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 31CH or MATH 109 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Applied Linear Algebra
courses.description: Second course in linear algebra from a computational yet geometric point of view. Elementary Hermitian matrices, Schur’s theorem, normal matrices, and quadratic forms. Moore-Penrose generalized inverse and least square problems. Vector and matrix norms. Characteristic and singular values. Canonical forms. Determinants and multilinear algebra.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 20F or MATH 31AH and MATH 20C. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Modern Algebra I
courses.description: First course in a two-quarter introduction to abstract algebra with some applications. Emphasis on group theory. Topics include definitions and basic properties of groups, properties of isomorphisms, subgroups. (Students may not receive credit for both MATH 100A and MATH 103A.)
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 31CH or MATH 109 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Number Theory I
courses.description: Elementary number theory with applications. Topics include unique factorization, irrational numbers, residue systems, congruences, primitive roots, reciprocity laws, quadratic forms, arithmetic functions, partitions, Diophantine equations, distribution of primes. Applications include fast Fourier transform, signal processing, codes, cryptography.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 100B or MATH 103B. Students who have not completed the listed prerequisite(s) may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Basic Number Theory
courses.description: The course will cover the basic arithmetic properties of the integers, with applications to Diophantine equations and elementary Diophantine approximation theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 31CH or MATH 109. Students who have not completed the listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Reasoning
courses.description: This course uses a variety of topics in mathematics to introduce the students to rigorous mathematical proof, emphasizing quantifiers, induction, negation, proof by contradiction, naive set theory, equivalence relations and epsilon-delta proofs. Required of all departmental majors.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 20F or MATH 31AH, and MATH 20C. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Modeling I
courses.description: An introduction to mathematical modeling in the physical and social sciences. Topics vary, but have included mathematical models for epidemics, chemical reactions, political organizations, magnets, economic mobility, and geographical distributions of species. May be taken for credit two times when topics change.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20D, MATH 18 or MATH 20F or MATH 31AH, and MATH 109 or MATH 31CH. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Elements of Complex Analysis
courses.description: Complex numbers and functions. Analytic functions, harmonic functions, elementary conformal mappings. Complex integration. Power series. Cauchy’s theorem. Cauchy’s formula. Residue theorem.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20E or MATH 31CH, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Foundations of Real Analysis I
courses.description: First course in a rigorous three-quarter sequence on real analysis. Topics include the real number system, basic topology, numerical sequences and series, continuity. (Students may not receive credit for both MATH 140A and MATH 142A.)
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 31CH or MATH 109. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Analysis I
courses.description: First course in an introductory two-quarter sequence on analysis. Topics include the real number system, numerical sequences and series, infinite limits, limits of functions, continuity, differentiation. Students may not receive credit for MATH 142A if taken after or concurrently with MATH 140A.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 31CH or MATH 109. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry
courses.description: Differential geometry of curves and surfaces. Gauss and mean curvatures, geodesics, parallel displacement, Gauss-Bonnet theorem.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20E or MATH 31CH and either MATH 18 or MATH 20F or MATH 31AH. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Applicable Mathematics and Computing
courses.description: This course will give students experience in applying theory to real world applications such as internet and wireless communication problems. The course will incorporate talks by experts from industry and students will be helped to carry out independent projects. Topics include graph visualization, labelling, and embeddings, random graphs and randomized algorithms. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20D and either MATH 18 or MATH 20F or MATH 31AH. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Geometry for Secondary Teachers
courses.description: Two- and three-dimensional Euclidean geometry is developed from one set of axioms. Pedagogical issues will emerge from the mathematics and be addressed using current research in teaching and learning geometry. This course is designed for prospective secondary school mathematics teachers.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 109 or MATH 31CH, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Discrete Mathematics and Graph Theory
courses.description: Basic concepts in graph theory, including trees, walks, paths, and connectivity, cycles, matching theory, vertex and edge-coloring, planar graphs, flows and combinatorial algorithms, covering Hall’s theorems, the max-flow min-cut theorem, Euler’s formula, and the travelling salesman problem. Credit not offered for MATH 154 if MATH 158 is previously taken. If MATH 154 and MATH 158 are concurrently taken, credit is only offered for MATH 158.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 31CH or MATH 109. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis: Linear Algebra
courses.description: This course covers analysis of numerical methods for linear algebraic systems and least squares problems. Topics include orthogonalization methods. Ill conditioned problems. Eigenvalue and singular value computations. Knowledge of programming recommended.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 31AH, and MATH 20C or MATH 31BH and CSE 20 or MATH 15A or MATH 31CH or MATH 109. Students who have not completed the listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Optimization Methods for Data Science I
courses.description: Introduction to convexity: convex sets, convex functions; geometry of hyperplanes; support functions for convex sets; hyperplanes and support vector machines. Linear and quadratic programming: optimality conditions; duality; primal and dual forms of linear support vector machines; active-set methods; interior methods. Students may not receive credit for both DSC 123A and MATH 173A.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20C or MATH 31BH and MATH 18 or 31AH. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Probability
courses.description: Probability spaces, random variables, independence, conditional probability, distribution, expectation, variance, joint distributions, central limit theorem. (Two units of credit offered for MATH 180A if ECON 120A previously, no credit offered if ECON 120A concurrently. Two units of credit offered for MATH 180A if MATH 183 or 186 taken previously or concurrently.) Prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 109 is highly recommended.
courses.prerequisites_text: Math 20C or MATH 31BH, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Stochastic Processes II
courses.description: Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, random walk, recurrent events. If time permits, topics chosen from stationary normal processes, branching processes, queuing theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 180B or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics II
courses.description: Hypothesis testing. Linear models, regression, and analysis of variance. Goodness of fit tests. Nonparametric statistics. Two units of credit offered for MATH 181B if ECON 120B previously; no credit offered if ECON 120B concurrently. Prior enrollment in MATH 109 is highly recommended.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 181A or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Statistical Methods
courses.description: Introduction to probability. Discrete and continuous random variables–binomial, Poisson and Gaussian distributions. Central limit theorem. Data analysis and inferential statistics: graphical techniques, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, curve fitting. (Credit not offered for MATH 183 if ECON 120A, ECE 109, MAE 108, MATH 181A, or MATH 186 previously or concurrently taken. Two units of credit offered for MATH 183 if MATH 180A taken previously or concurrently.)
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20C or MATH 31BH, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Enumerative Combinatorics
courses.description: Introduction to the theory and applications of combinatorics. Enumeration of combinatorial structures (permutations, integer partitions, set partitions). Bijections, inclusion-exclusion, ordinary and exponential generating functions. Renumbered from MATH 184A; credit not offered for MATH 184 if MATH 184A if previously taken. Credit not offered for MATH 184 if MATH 188 previously taken. If MATH 184 and MATH 188 are concurrently taken, credit only offered for MATH 188.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 31CH or MATH 109. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Cryptography
courses.description: An introduction to the basic concepts and techniques of modern cryptography. Classical cryptanalysis. Probabilistic models of plaintext. Monoalphabetic and polyalphabetic substitution. The one-time system. Caesar-Vigenere-Playfair-Hill substitutions. The Enigma. Modern-day developments. The Data Encryption Standard. Public key systems. Security aspects of computer networks. Data protection. Electronic mail. Recommended preparation: basic programming experience. Renumbered from MATH 187. Students may not receive credit for both MATH 187A and MATH 187.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or MATH 20A. Students who have not completed listed prerequisite may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics of Modern Cryptography
courses.description: The object of this course is to study modern public key cryptographic systems and cryptanalysis (e.g., RSA, Diffie-Hellman, elliptic curve cryptography, lattice-based cryptography, homomorphic encryption) and the mathematics behind them. We also explore other applications of these computational techniques (e.g., integer factorization and attacks on RSA). Recommended preparation: Familiarity with Python and/or mathematical software (especially SAGE) would be helpful, but it is not required.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 187A and MATH 18 or MATH 31AH. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebraic Combinatorics
courses.description: A rigorous introduction to algebraic combinatorics. Basic enumeration and generating functions. Enumeration involving group actions: Polya theory. Posets and Sperner property. q-analogs and unimodality. Partitions and tableaux. Credit not offered for MATH 188 if MATH 184 or MATH 184A previously taken. If MATH 184 and MATH 188 are concurrently taken, credit only offered for MATH 188.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 31CH or MATH 109 and MATH 18 or MATH 31AH and MATH 100A or 103A. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Exploratory Data Analysis and Inference
courses.description: An introduction to various quantitative methods and statistical techniques for analyzing data—in particular big data. Quick review of probability continuing to topics of how to process, analyze, and visualize data using statistical language R. Further topics include basic inference, sampling, hypothesis testing, bootstrap methods, and regression and diagnostics. Offers conceptual explanation of techniques, along with opportunities to examine, implement, and practice them in real and simulated data.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 20F or MATH 31AH, and MATH 20C and one of BENG 134, CSE 103, ECE 109, ECON 120A, MAE 108, MATH 180A, MATH 183, MATH 186, or SE 125. Students who have not completed listed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Foundations of Topology I
courses.description: An introduction to point set topology: topological spaces, subspace topologies, product topologies, quotient topologies, continuous maps and homeomorphisms, metric spaces, connectedness, compactness, basic separation, and countability axioms. Examples. Instructor may choose further topics such as Urysohn’s lemma, Urysohn’s metrization theorem. Formerly MATH 190. Students may not receive credit for MATH 190A and MATH 190.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 31CH or MATH 140A or MATH 142A. Students who have not completed prerequisites may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Student Colloquium
courses.description: A variety of topics and current research results in mathematics will be presented by guest lecturers and students under faculty direction. May be taken for P/NP grade only.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division status.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Extracurricular Industry Practicum
courses.description: An enrichment program which provides academic credit for work experience with public/private sector employers. After independently securing an internship with significant mathematical content, students will identify a faculty member to work with directly, discussing the mathematics involved. Faculty may require related readings and assignments as appropriate. May be taken for credit three times. Units may not be applied towards major graduation requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: permission of department.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading in advanced mathematics by individual students. Three periods. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: permission of department.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Honors Thesis Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Honors thesis research for seniors participating in the Honors Program. Research is conducted under the supervision of a mathematics faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Honors Program in mathematics, department stamp.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebra I
courses.description: First course in graduate algebra. Topics may include group actions, Sylow theorems, solvable and nilpotent groups, free groups and presentations, semidirect products, polynomial rings, unique factorization, chain conditions, modules over principal ideal domains, rational and Jordan canonical forms, tensor products, projective and flat modules, Galois theory, solvability by radicals, localization, primary decomposition, Hilbert Nullstellensatz, integral extensions, Dedekind domains, Krull dimension.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in MA75, MA76, MA77, MA80, MA81. All other students may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Applied Algebra I
courses.description: Introduction to algebra from a computational perspective. Groups, rings, linear algebra, rational and Jordan forms, unitary and Hermitian matrices, matrix decompositions, perturbation of eigenvalues, group representations, symmetric functions, fast Fourier transform, commutative algebra, Grobner basis, finite fields.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Algebraic Geometry I
courses.description: Introduction to algebraic geometry. Topics chosen from: varieties and their properties, sheaves and schemes and their properties. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 200C. Students who have not taken MATH 200C may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Number Theory I
courses.description: First course in graduate-level number theory. Local fields: valuations and metrics on fields; discrete valuation rings and Dedekind domains; completions; ramification theory; main statements of local class field theory. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 200C. Students who have not taken MATH 200C may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Algebraic Geometry
courses.description: Various topics in algebraic geometry. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. Nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor. (S/U grade only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Number Theory
courses.description: Various topics in number theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grade only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Algebra
courses.description: Various topics in algebra.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. Nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor. May be taken for credit nine times. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Mathematics of Biological Systems
courses.description: Various topics in the mathematics of biological systems. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Complex Analysis
courses.description: Complex numbers and functions. Cauchy theorem and its applications, calculus of residues, expansions of analytic functions, analytic continuation, conformal mapping and Riemann mapping theorem, harmonic functions. Dirichlet principle, Riemann surfaces.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 140A-B or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Partial Differential Equations I
courses.description: First course in graduate partial differential equations. Laplace, heat, and wave equations. Non-linear first order equations, including Hamilton-Jacobi theory. Sobolev spaces and initial/boundary value problems for linear elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic equations. Non-linear second order equations, including calculus of variations.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 210B or 240C. Students who have not completed MATH 210B or 240C may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Real Analysis I
courses.description: First course in graduate real analysis. Abstract measure and integration theory, integration on product spaces. Lebesgue measure and integral, Lebesgue-Stieltjes integrals, functions of bounded variation, differentiation of measures. Locally compact Hausdorff spaces, Banach and Hilbert spaces, linear functionals. Lebesgue spaces and interpolation, elements of Fourier analysis and distribution theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in MA75, MA76, MA77, MA80, MA81. All other students may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Functional Analysis
courses.description: Various topics in functional analysis. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Real Analysis
courses.description: Various topics in real analysis.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grade only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Differential Geometry
courses.description: Differential manifolds, Sard theorem, tensor bundles, Lie derivatives, DeRham theorem, connections, geodesics, Riemannian metrics, curvature tensor and sectional curvature, completeness, characteristic classes. Differential manifolds immersed in Euclidean space.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topics in Differential Geometry
courses.description: Introduction to varied topics in differential geometry. In recent years, topics have included Morse theory and general relativity. May be taken for credit six times with consent of adviser.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. Nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Differential Geometry
courses.description: Various topics in differential geometry. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grade only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Geometrical Physics
courses.description: Manifolds, differential forms, homology, deRham’s theorem. Riemannian geometry, harmonic forms. Lie groups and algebras, connections in bundles, homotopy sequence of a bundle, Chern classes. Applications selected from Hamiltonian and continuum mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, special and general relativity, Yang-Mills fields.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in mathematics, physics, or engineering, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Combinatorics
courses.description: Topics from partially ordered sets, Mobius functions, simplicial complexes and shell ability. Enumeration, formal power series and formal languages, generating functions, partitions. Lagrange inversion, exponential structures, combinatorial species. Finite operator methods, q-analogues, Polya theory, Ramsey theory. Representation theory of the symmetric group, symmetric functions and operations with Schur functions.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Combinatorics
courses.description: Various topics in combinatorics.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grade only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Linear Algebra
courses.description: Error analysis of the numerical solution of linear equations and least squares problems for the full rank and rank deficient cases. Error analysis of numerical methods for eigenvalue problems and singular value problems. Iterative methods for large sparse systems of linear equations.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Numerical Partial Differential Equations I
courses.description: Survey of discretization techniques for elliptic partial differential equations, including finite difference, finite element and finite volume methods. Lax-Milgram Theorem and LBB stability. A priori error estimates. Mixed methods. Convection-diffusion equations. Systems of elliptic PDEs.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Computational and Applied Mathematics
courses.description: Various topics in computational and applied mathematics.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. Nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor. (S/U grade only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Mathematics of Information, Data, and Signals
courses.description: Various topics in the mathematics of information, data, and signals.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grade only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Optimization
courses.description: Various topics in optimization and applications. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. (S/U grade only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Probability Theory I
courses.description: This is the first course in a three-course sequence in probability theory. Topics covered in the sequence include the measure-theoretic foundations of probability theory, independence, the Law of Large Numbers, convergence in distribution, the Central Limit Theorem, conditional expectation, martingales, Markov processes, and Brownian motion. Recommended preparation: completion of real analysis equivalent to MATH 140A-B strongly recommended.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematical Statistics
courses.description: Statistical models, sufficiency, efficiency, optimal estimation, least squares and maximum likelihood, large sample theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: advanced calculus and basic probability theory or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Applied Statistics I
courses.description: General theory of linear models with applications to regression analysis. Ordinary and generalized least squares estimators and their properties. Hypothesis testing, including analysis of variance, and confidence intervals. Completion of courses in linear algebra and basic statistics are recommended prior to enrollment.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Statistical Methods in Bioinformatics
courses.description: This course will cover material related to the analysis of modern genomic data; sequence analysis, gene expression/functional genomics analysis, and gene mapping/applied population genetics. The course will focus on statistical modeling and inference issues and not on database mining techniques.
courses.prerequisites_text: one year of calculus, one statistics course or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Stochastic Differential Equations
courses.description: Review of continuous martingale theory. Stochastic integration for continuous semimartingales. Existence and uniqueness theory for stochastic differential equations. Strong Markov property. Selected applications.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 280A-B or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Various topics in probability and statistics.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grade only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Topology
courses.description: Point set topology, including separation axioms, compactness, connectedness. Algebraic topology, including the fundamental group, covering spaces, homology and cohomology. Homotopy or applications to manifolds as time permits.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 100A-B-C and MATH 140A-B-C.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Seminar in Topology
courses.description: Various topics in topology. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grade only.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Special Topics in Mathematics
courses.description: A variety of topics and current research results in mathematics will be presented by staff members and students under faculty direction.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics Graduate Research Internship
courses.description: An enrichment program that provides work experience with public/private sector employers and researchers. Under supervision of a faculty adviser, students provide mathematical consultation services. May be taken up to three times for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Reading and Research
courses.description: Independent study and research for the doctoral dissertation. One to three credits will be given for independent study (reading) and one to nine for research.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Teaching Assistant Training
courses.description: A course in which teaching assistants are aided in learning proper teaching methods through faculty-led discussions, preparation and grading of examinations and other written exercises, academic integrity, and student interactions. Number of units for credit depends on number of hours devoted to teaching assistant duties. May be taken for credit up to nine times for a maximum of thirty-six units. Must have concurrent teaching assistant appointment in mathematics.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of adviser. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: MATS
courses.title: Graduate Seminar
courses.description: Each graduate student in the Materials Science and Engineering Program is expected to attend a weekly seminar in materials science or related areas. MS students must enroll for three quarters, PhD students for six quarters. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: MATS
courses.title: Thermodynamics of Solids
courses.description: The thermodynamics and statistical mechanics of solids. Basic concepts; equilibrium properties of alloy systems; thermodynamic information from phase diagrams, surfaces, and interfaces; crystalline defects.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. (Cross-listed with ECE 238A, MAE 271A, NANO 265.)

courses.subject: MATS
courses.title: MATS Academy I
courses.description: This course focuses on essential topics for student success and the development of soft skills critical to thriving in a graduate program. Throughout the course, students will engage with various campus resources and support services to strengthen their academic performance, time management, and professional development. By the end of the course, students will be equipped with strategies to navigate the challenges of graduate studies and to make the most of their educational experience.

courses.subject: MATS
courses.title: Structure and Analysis of Solids
courses.description: Key concepts in the atomic structure and bonding of solids such as metals, ceramics, and semiconductors. Symmetry operations, point groups, lattice types, space groups, simple and complex inorganic compounds, structure/property comparisons, structure determination with X-ray diffraction. Ionic, covalent, metallic bonding compared with physical properties. Atomic and molecular orbitals, bands verses bonds, free electron theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate student or consent of instructor. (Cross-listed with CHEM 222, MAE 251, NANO 227.)

courses.subject: MATS
courses.title: Electronic and Photonic Properties of Materials
courses.description: The electronic and optical properties of metals, semiconductors, and insulators. The concept of the band structure. Electronic and lattice conductivity. Type I and Type II superconductivity. Optical engineering using photonic band gap crystals in one-, two-, and three-dimensions. Current research frontiers.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of the instructor. (Cross-listed with MAE 265A.)

courses.subject: MATS
courses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering
courses.description: Quantitative basic understanding of different branches of polymer science varying from polymer chemistry, characterization, thermodynamics, rheological properties, smart materials, self-assembly in biopolymers (natural) and synthetic polymers, and applications of polymers ranging from medicine to structure.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. (Cross-listed with BENG 242, NANO 257, MAE 257.)

courses.subject: MATS
courses.title: Research Conference
courses.description: Group discussion of research activities and progress of group members.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MATS
courses.title: Graduate Research
courses.description: Subject to the approval of a faculty adviser, students may choose courses offered by departments participating in the Materials Science and Engineering Program. Please see the graduate coordinator for more information.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Critical Writing
courses.description: First course of sequence in university reading and writing which satisfies the Muir College graduation requirement in writing. Required of all Muir College first-year students and of transfer students who have not completed a comparable course elsewhere. MCWP 40 introduces students to the basic elements of argument and analysis. Students engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. Grades of C or higher are required for prerequisites. Students must take MCWP 40 for a letter grade to count toward the Muir College writing requirement. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MCWP 40, MCWP 40R, MCWP 40C, or MCWP 40CR.
courses.prerequisites_text: satisfaction of Entry Level Writing Requirement.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: CritWrit: Climate Change
courses.description: First course of sequence which satisfies the Muir College graduation requirement in writing. Required of all Muir College first-year students and of transfer students who have not completed a comparable course elsewhere. MCWP 40C introduces students to the basic elements of argument and analysis with a focus on climate change. Students engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. Satisfies the Jane Teranes Climate Change Education Requirement. Grades of C or higher are required for prerequisites. Students must take MCWP 40C for a letter grade to count toward the Muir College writing requirement. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MCWP 40, MCWP 40R, MCWP 40C, or MCWP 40CR.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Critical Writing
courses.description: Online version of the first course of sequence in university reading and writing which satisfies the Muir College graduation requirement in writing. Required of all Muir College first-year students and of transfer students who have not completed a comparable course elsewhere. MCWP 40R introduces students to the basic elements of argument and analysis. Students engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. This class is held synchronously online. Grades of C or higher are required for prerequisites. Must take MCWP 40R for a letter grade for the Muir College writing requirement. Credit given for only one of the following: MCWP 40, MCWP 40R, MCWP 40C, or MCWP 40CR. This is a distance education course.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Critical Writing
courses.description: Second course of sequence in reading and writing which satisfies the Muir College graduation requirement in writing. Required of all Muir College first-year students and of transfer students. MCWP 50 focuses on advanced skills of argument and analysis. Students engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. Students will not receive credit for both MCWP 50 and MCWP 50R. Must be taken for a letter grade to satisfy the Muir College writing requirement.
courses.prerequisites_text: satisfaction of the MCWP 40 requirement or completion of IGETC.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Argument and Analysis
courses.description: An advanced course in argumentation and analysis, with particular attention both to constructing arguments and analyzing the logic and rhetoric of others’ arguments. Students will engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. MCWP 125 courses are for transfer students who enter Muir College with TAG or IGETC. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MCWP 125, MCWP 125R, MCWP 50, or MCWP 50R. Course must be taken for letter grade to fulfill Muir College writing requirement.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Business
courses.description: Introduction to techniques to develop/analyze data for informed tactical and strategic management decisions: statistical inference, probability, regression analysis, and optimization. Using these analytic approaches, theory-based formulas, and spreadsheets, students explore managerial applications across all areas of business activity.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.description: Cross-listed with ECON 4. Recording, organizing, and communicating financial information to business entities.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Managerial Accounting
courses.description: Internal accounting fundamentals, including cost behavior, cost application methods, overhead allocation methods, break-even analysis, budgeting, cost variance analysis, inventory management, and capital budgeting.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Personal Financial Management
courses.description: Course examines management of personal financial assets: savings and checking accounts, fixed assets, and credit cards. Budgeting, loan applications, payment terms, and statement reconciliation will be covered as will credit ratings, cash management, compound interest, bank operations, and contract obligations.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Personal Ethics at Work
courses.description: Course examines the ethical foundation for choices individuals make every day both in the workplace and in their private lives, the connection between economic and ethical obligations with examples related to privacy, reporting, whistle-blowing, workplace relationships, confidentiality, and intellectual property.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Managing Diverse Teams
courses.description: The modern workplace includes people different in culture, gender, age, language, religion, education, and more. Students will learn why diverse teams make better decisions and are often integral to the success of organizations. Topics include challenges of diversity, and the impact of emotional, social, and cultural intelligence on team success. Content will include significant attention to the experiences of Asian Americans and African Americans as members and leaders of such diverse teams. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 18 and MGT 18GS.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Principles of Accounting
courses.description: Covers the principles, methods and applications of general accounting, cost accounting and investment ROI. Development of the three key financial reports and their interrelations, cost identification, product costing, inventory control, operational performance, and investment return

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Test and Measurement in the Workplace
courses.description: This course introduces students to the psychometric, legal, ethical, and practical considerations of using tests and measurements for evidence-based decision-making in the workplace. Emphasis is given to selection and performance measurements for individual, team, business unit and organization-wide use in marketing, STEM, and operations. Student teams will develop managerial recommendations following company specific research and analysis.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Operating a Successful Business
courses.description: Operating a business is a complex task but a skill that can be mastered. Business managers make interconnected decisions to bring products and services to market. How many workers should a burrito chain employ given demand projections and which burrito-building tasks should be completed before a customer walks in? When a bakery makes pastries, how many at a time? Why do airlines overbook? Managers must answer these questions to keep operations lean and outdo competitors. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 71 and MGT 71R.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Operating a Successful Business
courses.description: Operating a business is a complex task but a skill that can be mastered. Business managers make interconnected decisions to bring products and services to market. How many workers should a burrito chain employ given demand projections and which burrito-building tasks should be completed before a customer walks in? When a bakery makes pastries, how many at a time? Why do airlines overbook? Managers must answer these questions to keep operations lean and outdo competitors. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 71R and MGT 71. This course is a distance education course.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Customer Analytics
courses.description: Marketers use empirical models to determine, support, and evaluate a wide range of business decisions. This course covers models and estimation techniques commonly used for understanding segmentation, targeting, and positioning; product diffusion; advertising response, among other topics. Recommended preparation: ECON 120A. Familiarity with R will be assumed.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and BENG 100 or COGS 14B or ECE 109 or ECON 120A or MAE 108 or MATH 11 or MATH 180A or MATH 183 or MATH 186 or MGT 3 or PSYC 60 or SIO 187.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: E-Commerce
courses.description: E-commerce is the online exchange of information leading to mutually beneficial transactions. Students will learn and apply skills related to business opportunity ideation and evaluation, customer and market research, sourcing, fulfillment, positioning, pricing, branding, storytelling, store design, user experience testing, website analytics, search engine optimization, social media, content marketing, digital advertising, and online experimentation.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Product Marketing and Management
courses.description: Defining markets for products and services, segmenting these markets, and targeting critical customers within segments. Strategies to position products and services within segments. The critical role of pricing as well as market research, product management, promotion, selling, and customer support.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Product Promotion and Brand Management
courses.description: Principles and decisions to be considered in overall communications and promotion strategy for traditional channels and emerging social networks. Decisions on promotional mix, ad design, implementation and evaluation for establishing brand equity, measure brand performance and sustaining brand equity.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 100 or MGT 103.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Applied Market Research
courses.description: The business world revolves around managerial decisions, and those ought to be data driven. In this course we will learn about planning, implementing, and analyzing market research; synthesizing multi-methods research; and presenting market research results by actually doing it. We will learn how to plan and conduct interviews; how to design, execute, and analyze surveys; and how to employ cutting-edge tools such as adaptive conjoint analysis to quantify attribute levels and trade-offs. This course is a distance education course.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Topics in Marketing
courses.description: Introduces advanced topics of special interest in marketing. Topics may include advertising, consumer behavior, pricing, product life cycles, etc. This course may also cover the unique demands of innovation-driven, biotech, and high-technology markets. May be taken for credit no more than three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 100 or MGT 103, upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Global Business Strategy
courses.description: Will examine the advantages and complications of the multinational organization with emphasis on translating marketing, financing, and operating plans in light of geographical, cultural, and legal differences across the globe. Will also cover organizational considerations for transglobal management.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 100 or MGT 103 and MGT 180 or MGT 181 or MGT 187, upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Topics in Business
courses.description: Introduces advanced topics of special interest in business and addresses the new frontiers in the industry. Topics may include intellectual property, consumer behavior, market research, analytics, and spreadsheet modeling, etc. May be taken for credit three times. Instructional methods include face-to-face lecture, case presentation, assigned reading, and group discussion.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Innovation to Market A
courses.description: Consider new project concepts. Discern market needs, competitive environment, and determine “go to market” strategy. Research potential markets, customers, partners, and competitors. Consider price versus attributes, alternative distribution channels, gaining unfair advantage. Examine the need and structure of a start-up team.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: AI and Technology Strategy
courses.description: Focusing on how AI will redefine businesses in the digital age, we’ll study the fundamental topics of innovation driven by AI+X revolution, disruptive technologies, and digital transformation; learn the TOE theory and S curves to discriminate between trends and fads; how to make decisions about investment in technologies and new ventures, and look into the game changers in many industries (e.g., hi-tech, finance, healthcare), preparing students to become leaders in the tech-intensive world. Credit will not be allowed for MGT 127R and MGT 127.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Intermediate Accounting A
courses.description: Preparation and interpretation of accounting information under both FASB and IASB guidelines pertaining to revenue and expense recognition, receivables, and inventories.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and MGT 5 and and ECON 4 or MGT 4 or MGT 45.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Auditing
courses.description: Theory and practice of the attest process; planning and implementing the audit of the financial statements and internal control over financial reporting to ensure compliance with applicable requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 131B.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Federal Taxation—Companies
courses.description: Covers the theory and practical application of federal income tax regulations for corporations and other enterprises pertaining to formulations, annual operations, distributions, liquidations, reorganizations, affiliations, and reporting standards.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 131B.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Financial Statement Analysis
courses.description: Examines tools and techniques to analyze a firm’s financial position and performance. This course combines both accounting and finance in a practical framework for debt and equity valuation methods from both a conceptual and practical framework.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and MGT 45 or MGT 5 and ECON 4 or MGT 4 or MGT 45.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Business Analytics
courses.description: This course focuses on the concept of data analytics, and the convergence of data and business. From a practical standpoint, the course focuses on solving business problems by examining industry data, machine learning, statistics, and various forms of data analytics concepts. The fundamental goal of the course is to ensure students learn and understand fundamental interconnections and practical coding applications within the field of data analytics. This course is a distance education course. No credit for MGT 151R if taken after MGT 151A.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or MATH 18 or MATH 20A or MATH 31AH and BENG 100 or BIEB 100 or COGS 14B or ECE 109 or ECON 120A or MAE 108 or MATH 11 or MATH 180A or MATH 180B or MATH 181A or MATH 183 or MATH 186 or MGT 3 or PSYC 60 or SIO 187.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Information Technology in Business Analytics
courses.description: This course is designed to help a business manager use data to make good decisions in complex decision-making situations. Students will learn core business analytics concepts and skills including Excel, relational databases and Structured Query Language (SQL), principles of effective data visualizations and interactive data visualization (e.g., Tableau), and data preprocessing and regression analysis using data analytics programming (e.g., Python).
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or MATH 18 or MATH 20A or MATH 31AH and BENG 100 or BIEB 100 or COGS 14B or ECE 109 or ECON 120A or MAE 108 or MATH 11 or MATH 180A or MATH 181A or MATH 183 or MATH 186 or MGT 3 or PSYC 60 or SIO 187, upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Experiments in Firms
courses.description: An understanding of how to design and run a good experiment will position students at the cutting edge of decision-making in business and policy. Students will develop their own experiments that can be implemented online and in organizations. Students will learn to distinguish between a correlation and a causal effect; incorporate behavioral economics into experimental designs; randomize, analyze, and critique experimental interventions; and address organizational concerns about experimentation.
courses.prerequisites_text: (BENG 100 or BIEB 100 or COGS 14B or ECE 109 or ECON 120A or MAE 108 or MATH 11 or MATH 180A or MATH 181A or MATH 183 or MATH 186 or MGT 3 or PSYC 60 or SIO 187) and (MATH 10A or MATH 18 or MATH 20A or MATH 31AH).

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Negotiations
courses.description: This course takes a decision-making orientation to negotiation. The course will build cumulatively from (seemingly) simple negotiations to those of greater complexity. These structured negotiation exercises are used to isolate and emphasize specific analytic points and essential skills. Cases and readings should help the student to integrate the analysis as well as to develop intuition about more complex negotiations. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 162 and MGT 162R.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Negotiations
courses.description: This course takes a decision-making orientation to negotiation. The course will build cumulatively from (seemingly) simple negotiations to those of greater complexity. These structured negotiation exercises are used to isolate and emphasize specific analytic points and essential skills. Cases and readings should help the student integrate the analysis as well as to develop intuition about more complex negotiations. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 162R and MGT 162. This course is a distance education course.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Business and Organizational Leadership
courses.description: Students will study alternative organizational structures—their stakeholders and corporate cultures, and their use in meeting strategic enterprise priorities facing a company. This course provides students with insights into motivational factors, communications networks, organizational cultures, and alternative leadership styles. The concept of change management and its challenges is also studied along with power and influence. Students may not receive credit for MGT 164 and MGT 164GS. Course previously listed as: Organizational Leadership.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Business Ethics and Corporate Responsibility
courses.description: Will cover ethical conduct issues for leaders from a wide array of organizations and industries including consideration of differences among global trading partners. The issues impacting corporate responsibility will be examined as will full-cycle cost analysis of products and services.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Social Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Social entrepreneurs create innovative solutions to solve challenging social and environmental issues affecting the world around them. In this course, students will learn how to apply entrepreneurial business and innovative skills to effectively tackle global issues impacting society such as environmental degradation, rural health care availability, educational improvements in economically disadvantaged regions of the world, famine in an era of obesity, and clean water development.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Business Project Management
courses.description: Addresses effective practices for management of business projects. Includes both project management processes—scheduling, milestone setting, resource allocation, budgeting, risk mitigation—and human capital management—communication, teamwork, leadership. Also considers requirements for effectively working across functional and organizational boundaries. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 172 and MGT 172R.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Project Management: Health Services
courses.description: This course covers efficient techniques for managing health services projects, including both the technical aspects of project management as well as the human-capital management issues associated with blending administrative and technical staff with health-care professionals. Topics include scheduling methods, milestone setting, governmental regulations, resource allocation, interpersonal skills, and performing research and development projects—all with a health services focus.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Supply chain management involves the flows of materials and information that contribute value to a product, from the source of raw materials to end customers. This course explains how supply chains work and describes the major challenges in managing an efficient supply chain. Covers various strategic and tactical supply chain issues such as distribution strategy, information sharing strategy, outsourcing, procurement (including e-markets), product design, virtual integration, and risk management. Credit is not allowed for both MGT 174 and MGT 175.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Business Finance
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the fundamental concepts in corporate finance. Topics include discounted cash flow, capital budgeting, bond and stock valuation, portfolio theory, market efficiency, the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), the determinants of capital structure and options. We will seek a balance between theoretical paradigms, the empirical facts, and their applicability to real-world issues. Emphasis will be placed on general principles and problem solving. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 180 and MGT 180R.
courses.prerequisites_text: ECE 109 or ECON 100A or ECON 120A or MAE 108 or MATH 180A or MATH 183 or MATH 186.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Enterprise Finance
courses.description: Will cover debt and equity financing of the enterprise, the role of commercial banks, venture firms, and investment banks; along with enterprise valuation, cash flow management, capital expenditure decisions, return on investment, economic value add, and foreign currency translation.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and (MATH 10A or MATH 20A or MGT 3) and (MGT 5 or MGT 45) and (MGT 4 or MGT 45 or ECON 4).

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Financial Investments
courses.description: Examines financial theory and empirical evidence useful for making investment decisions. Portfolio theory, equilibrium models, and market efficiency are examined for stock securities and fixed income instruments. Risk adjusted ROIs for capital investments’ impact on stock prices and free options will also be studied.
courses.prerequisites_text: ECON 173B or MGT 180 or MGT 180R or MGT 181 or MGT 187.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: New Venture Finance
courses.description: Taking a global perspective, this course examines how innovation is funded and the financial tools necessary over the life cycle of a new venture—development, growth, maturity, and exit. Students will learn to perform financial analysis to determine the feasibility of financing new, transformed, and growing ventures, whether foreign or domestic. The course will also cover term sheets, valuation methods, and the role of private equity investors—angels, VCs, and vendors.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Topics in Finance
courses.description: Introduces advanced topics of special interest in finance. Topics may include behavioral finance, financial derivatives, portfolio management, fixed income securities, asset pricing theory, commercial banking, etc. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 180 or MGT 180R or MGT 181 or MGT 187, upper-division standing .

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: A small group undertaking, on a topic or in a field not included in the regular curriculum, by special arrangement with a faculty member. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and instructor consent and department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Directed Independent Study
courses.description: Directed individual study or research by special arrangement and under supervision of a faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and department approval; approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Behavioral Economics
courses.description: Introduction to formal and predictive approaches to incorporating behavioral regularities into economic theory. Covers developments in generalizing conventional economic models to allow patterns of behavior that appear to be common but are paradoxical for conventional models based on assumptions of rationality.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 208A-B-C, ECON 200A-B-C.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Statistical Programming and Data Inference I
courses.description: This course covers foundational topics in statistical programming in the social sciences using the statistical language R. No prior programming knowledge is required. Topics may include data visualization, probability, measurement, causal inference, and an emphasis on the flexible statistical framework of the generalized linear model.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to management PhD program or by consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Psychology and Decision Making
courses.description: This course introduces students to theories and research in the field of individual judgment and decision making. Topics include judgment under uncertainty, the psychology of risk, choice, decision framing, prospect theory, mental accounting, context effects, task effects, and regret.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to management PhD program or by consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Topics in Marketing Research
courses.description: This course will discuss key papers and findings in the marketing literature to make the students experts in the field. The course will require students to build on the papers discussed and to prepare students for their independent research.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to management PhD program or by consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Dissertation
courses.description: This course is taken by students actively working on their dissertation after advancing to candidacy.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Advanced Field Advising
courses.description: Each student who has not advanced to candidacy by June of the third year must enroll in and complete MGT 299 during the fall, winter, and spring quarters of the fourth year.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to management PhD program.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Business Analytics for Managers
courses.description: Through lecture and online delivery, students will be introduced to key techniques for using data to make informed management decisions. Covers probability, statistics, decision analysis, and optimization techniques. Emphasizes managerial applications in such areas as operations management, marketing, and finance. Letter grades only. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 403 and MGT 403R.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.description: Through lecture and online delivery, students will be introduced to key techniques for using data to make informed management decisions. Covers probability, statistics, decision analysis, and optimization techniques. Emphasizes managerial applications in such areas as operations management, marketing, and finance. Letter grades only. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 403R and MGT 403. This is a distance education course.
courses.prerequisites_text: Executive MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Accounting
courses.description: Through lecture and online delivery, students will be introduced to the basic concepts and methods used in financial statements. The course highlights the linkages between accounting information and management planning, decision making, and control. Letter grades only. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MGT 404, MGT 404R, or MGTF 401.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Managerial Economics
courses.description: Introduction to the use of microeconomics in managerial decision-making. Examines how the optimal strategy of a firm is impacted by the structure of the market, the competitive and regulatory constraints, and the structure of information. Topics include supply and demand analysis, price discrimination techniques, contractual relationships, and asymmetric information. Students learn to apply economic principles to solving business problems and the importance of marginal analysis in decisions. Letter grades only. Students will not receive credit for both MGT 405 and MGT 405R.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Leading People
courses.description: Through lecture and online delivery, introduces principles of effective teamwork and leadership and of strategic managerial communication. Provides an introduction to case study and to ethical issues confronting managers in technology or science-driven firms. Develops managerial communication skills. Letter grades only. Students will not earn credit for both MGT 406 and MGT 406R.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Strategy
courses.description: Through lecture and online delivery, this course explores the strategic management of technology-driven firms focusing on the analytical tools and techniques that support strategy formulation and the related managerial skills and decision processes that foster strategy implementation. Letter grades only. Students may not receive credit for both MGT 410 and MGT 410R.

Letter grades only. Students may not receive credit for both MGT 410R and MGT 410. This is a distance education course.
courses.prerequisites_text: Executive MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.title: New Venture Design

courses.prerequisites_text: Executive MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Rady Action Project
courses.description: Rady action project core course provides students with the opportunity to integrate and apply foundational skills by working on a consulting project that tackles a real-world business problem confronted by a local firm. No credit for MGT 414R if taken after MGT 414. This is a distance education course.
courses.prerequisites_text: Executive MBA student or by instructor approval or by department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Negotiation
courses.description: Examines methods of conflict resolution needed for effective management in a constantly changing business environment. Applies these tools to the broad spectrum of negotiation problems faced by the manager and professional. Includes simulations, role playing, and cases. Students may not earn credit for both MGT 420 and MGT 420R.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Supply Chain Cost Management Strategy
courses.description: Provides students with a comprehensive understanding of world-class supply management processes, data sources and processes to develop cost models, and a structured process to create and implement cost management strategies. Students learn through industry leader guest speakers and real-life examples of concept implementation at various Fortune 100 companies.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 413 and MBA student or by instructor approval or by department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Spreadsheet Modeling
courses.description: The course will provide students with knowledge and techniques to apply management science principles and spreadsheet modeling to support decision-making under various business scenarios. Students will learn and understand the fundamentals of analytical modeling, understand business problems and convert them to analytical models, build spreadsheet models, and effectively deliver managerial implications derived from computer models.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGT 413 and MBA student or by instructor approval or by department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: AI and Disruptive Technology Strategy

courses.title: Valuation in Corporate Finance
courses.description: Covering the fundamentals of corporate finance and their application to valuation (including the WACC approach, APV approach, multiples and real option valuation). We focus on important areas of corporate finance, including capital structure, real options, and financial distress and bankruptcy. Students may not receive credit for both MGT 487 and MGTF 407.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

We will do this by actually doing it.
