This course is a distance education course.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Mergers, Acquisitions, and Corporate Restructurings
courses.description: Explains the mergers and acquisitions process. Topics include history, motivation, valuation, legal framework and tax issues of M&A, anti-takeover strategies, takeover tactics, leveraged buyouts, joint venture, and strategic alliances. Students may not receive credit for both MGT 490 and MGTF 409.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: New Venture Finance
courses.description: Focuses on the financing of new ventures and technological innovation. Includes perspectives of both the entrepreneur and the investor, including the venture capital process and methods of financial valuation useful in the venture capital industry and for other technology investments. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MGT 493R or MGT 493 or MGTF 410. This is a distance education course.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Advanced Management Research Practicum
courses.description: Internship with approved business or governmental agency, allowing student to pursue topics raised in the management core and elective courses. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit four times, for a maximum of four units, with instructor consent. Students may not earn credit for both MGT 497 and MGT 297. Internship credit may not be applied to fulfill specific course requirements or to credits required for graduation.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Individual Directed Study
courses.description: Individual study or research under the direction of a selected faculty member. May be taken for credit twelve times. Students may earn credit for a total of twelve units in MGT 299 and/or MGT 499.
courses.prerequisites_text: MBA student or consent of instructor and department stamp.

courses.subject: MGTA
courses.title: Data Driven Communications
courses.description: This project-based course explores and develops applied communication skills needed for analytical professions to make the business case. Students work individually and in teams to develop persuasive messaging to communicate complex technical information and business insights to, and between, technical experts and business decision-makers.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics students or with department and instructor approval.

courses.subject: MGTA
courses.title: Collecting and Analyzing Large Data
courses.description: This course aims to provide students with an introduction to data analytics in R where the emphasis is more on business “data” than “analytics.” The emphasis is on collecting, handling, manipulating, and summarizing large data sets. Case studies are used throughout the course.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGTA 451 and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

courses.subject: MGTA
courses.title: Business Analytics
courses.description: This course is designed to help a business manager to use data to make good decisions in complex decision-making situations. Several analytical and econometric methods will be covered including decision analysis, regression analysis, optimization, and simulation.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGTA 451 and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

courses.subject: MGTA
courses.title: Business Intelligence Systems
courses.description: A decision support system consists of decision model, data, and user interface. This course covers the R and Shiny programming and design skills to develop a DSS that addresses a manager’s decision-making needs.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

courses.subject: MGTA
courses.title: Managerial Judgment and Decision-Making
courses.description: Decision making is difficult with scarce resources, inexact information, and conflicting stakeholder agendas (i.e., most of the time). Students will use advanced behavioral research to gain a competitive advantage, by improving their decisions and their understanding of how others decide.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGTA 451, MGTA 452, MGTA 453, and restricted to MS in business analytics program or with department and instructor approval.

courses.subject: MGTA
courses.title: Web Mining and Recommender Systems
courses.description: A graduate course devoted to current methods for recommender systems, data mining, and predictive analytics.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Financial Accounting
courses.description: Overview of financial accounting reporting, with a primary focus on the analysis of economic events and their effect on the major financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cash flows). Learn the nature and purpose of accounting methods. Letter grades only. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MGTF 401, MGT 404, or MGT 404R.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Investment Analysis
courses.description: Introduces quantitative methods for analyzing the pricing and return behavior of assets such as stocks, bonds, and derivatives; and develops methods for implementing modern portfolio theory in practice. The most influential financial models are derived; their practical applications are discussed. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Financial Econometrics and Empirical Methods
courses.description: Bridging the gap between theoretical financial models and the real world. Covering the major accomplishments of empirical finance. Empirical exercises and analysis of real financial data will help students to truly appreciate the content of the course. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Business Forecasting
courses.description: Introduction to state-of-the-art forecasting methods in finance. Students will learn to estimate forecasting models based on past values of the predicted variable(s), surveys, market information, and other economic data. Participants will become critical consumers of forecasts reported in the media. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Collecting and Analyzing Financial Data
courses.description: Teaches students how to obtain and process data in order to answer empirical questions in finance. The data can be numerical or textual, and structured or unstructured. Specific data sources may include CRSP, Compustat, Thomson Reuters, and Bloomberg. Some programming. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Preparing for the CFA Exam
courses.description: The Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) designation is the industry-accepted gold standard for financial analysts. To earn the CFA charter, students must pass three very challenging exams. Students will look at each of the ten major topic areas and explore the level of understanding that is required to pass the first-level exam. Students will do applied valuation work as well as highlight study habits of successful past candidates.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Capstone: Applied Finance Project
courses.description: The Capstone project is one of the primary measures of student learning. Evaluation is based on students’ ability to apply course material to the Capstone project. Satisfactory completion of the project is required for award of the degree. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGTF 402, MGTF 403, MGTF 404, and restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTP
courses.title: Professional Seminar
courses.description: Professional Seminar presents current industry research, professional skills development, and industry experts and business leaders as speakers. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to MPAc students (major code RS91) or by department approval.

courses.subject: MGTP
courses.title: Business Law
courses.description: Focuses on elements of business law that are essential for the basic management of business operations. Topics include the law of contracts, sales, partnership, corporations, securities, accountants’ legal liability, and Sarbanes Oxley statutes.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to MPAc students (major code RS91) or by department approval.

courses.subject: MGTP
courses.title: Internal Control over Financial Reporting
courses.description: Examines internal control from both an internal and external audit perspective, including control frameworks, improved information technology, role of corporate governance and audit committees, corporate risk management, SOX 404, internal auditing, and forensic auditing.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to MPAc students (major code RS91) or by department approval.

courses.subject: MGTP
courses.title: Professional Communications for Accountants
courses.description: The course develops essential communication skills for accounting professionals, focusing on written and oral presentations, teamwork, and interpersonal communication. It provides targeted instruction tailored to the unique needs of the accounting field, enabling students to effectively convey complex financial information. This class prepares students to meet the communication demands of the profession, fostering confidence, clarity, and collaboration in their roles.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to MPAc students (major code RS91) or by department approval.

courses.subject: MGTP
courses.title: Professional Research for Accountants
courses.description: This course is designed to meet state board requirements for focused instruction on accounting and tax research. It equips students with skills to analyze authoritative literature using tools like RIA Checkpoint and CCH IntelliConnect, emphasizing practical application of the IRAC framework to real-world accounting issues.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to MPAc students (major code RS91) or by department approval.

courses.subject: MGTP
courses.title: Advanced Auditing and Forensic Accounting
courses.description: Provides students with applied knowledge on how assurance professionals assess and evaluate assurance-related evidence and risks. Topics include strategic risk analysis, corporate governance, internal control assessments, audit sampling, modified audit reports, and fraud detection.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to MPAc students (major code RS91) or by department approval.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: Prehistory and Ancient Foundations
courses.description: This course explores human origins, the development of early forms of social and political organization, the strategies that early societies used to negotiate their physical and social environments, and the appearance of influential cultural traditions across the ancient world (to circa 100 BCE). Topics include the emergence of agriculture, the relationship between nomad and settled, the birth of the city and the expanding human “footprint,” the development of writing, foundational religious and cosmological ideas and narratives, influential models of visual and material culture, and changing forms of social stratification and inequality. Students may not receive credit for both MMW 11 and MMW 11R. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: Divergent Paths to the Modern World, Eighteenth–Twentieth Century
courses.description: This course explores divergent paths to modernity between the mid-eighteenth century and World War I. The course examines the influence of “the West” as a hegemonic force that disrupted global connections and forged new ones, changing the social, economic, political, and ecological norms of societies worldwide. The course investigates how groups and individuals around the world adopted, contested, and/or resisted this influence. Students may receive credit for MMW 14 with any one of the following: MMW 14, MMW 14R, or MMW 14GS. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement.
courses.prerequisites_text: MMW 12 or MMW 12R and MMW 13 or MMW 13R with a grade of D or better.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: The Contemporary Era: Conflict and Aspirations in a Globalized World, Twentieth–Twenty-First Century
courses.description: This course explores the sociocultural, economic, and political forces that shaped the twentieth and twenty-first century and contestations over them, with particular focus on the complex interaction between humans and the natural world. It examines the overlapping causes and impact of the global and local conflicts and inequalities that have defined the contemporary era. The course addresses efforts to defend and expand freedom, improve quality of life, and increase transnational cooperation and communication that challenge those hierarchies that perpetuate inequality. The course reflects on what this recent history may mean for our collective future. Students may receive credit for MMW 15 with any one of the following: MMW 15, MMW 15R, or MMW 15GS. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement. Satisfies the Jane Teranes Climate Change Education Requirement.
courses.prerequisites_text: MMW 12 or MMW 12R and MMW 13 or MMW 13R with a grade of D or better.

courses.subject: MMW
courses.title: Exploring the Modern World
courses.description: This course addresses specific themes and topics from the modern world (from the eighteenth century to the present) and strengthens transfer students’ analytical, research, and writing skills. Students may not receive credit for both MMW 122 and MMW 122R. Open to Eleanor Roosevelt College (ERC) transfer students only. Must be taken for a letter grade to meet the ERC graduation requirement.

courses.subject: MSED
courses.title: MSED Orientation Practicum
courses.description: Each practicum lasts five weeks and is designed to inform students about a faculty member’s research program. Assignment as a research assistant may be used as one practicum. This course should be taken during the first year. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to MSED Joint Doctoral Program. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: MSED
courses.title: Reading and Research
courses.description: Students will do independent study and research in preparation of their doctoral dissertation under the supervision of MSED faculty.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Fundamentals of Music A
courses.description: This course, first in a three-quarter sequence, is primarily intended for students without previous musical experience. It introduces music notation and basic music theory topics such as intervals, scales, keys, and chords, as well as basic rhythm skills.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Basic Musicianship
courses.description: Primarily intended for music majors. Development of basic skills: perception and notation of pitch and temporal relationships. Introduction to functional harmony. Studies in melodic writing. Drills in sight singing, rhythmic reading, and dictation.
courses.prerequisites_text: passing score on proficiency exam or consent of instructor. Must be taken in sequence. Music majors must be concurrently enrolled in MUS 2AK, 2BK, and 2CK (Basic Keyboard).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Basic Keyboard
courses.description: Scales, chords, harmonic progressions, transposition, and simple pieces.
courses.prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in MUS 2A, B, C.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Electronic Music
courses.description: Lectures and listening sessions devoted to the most significant works of music realized through the use of computers and other electronic devices from the middle of this century through the present.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: American Music: Jazz Cultures
courses.description: Jazz is one of the primary foundations for American music in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. This course highlights the multicultural and international scope of jazz by taking a thematic rather than a chronological approach to the subject, and by highlighting the music and lives of a diverse array of jazz practitioners from around the country and around the world. Students may not receive credit for both MUS 8 and MUS 8GS.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. (Offered in selected years.)

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Opera
courses.description: A study of works from the history of opera to coincide when possible with operas presented in the San Diego opera season. Class consists of lectures, listening labs, live performances, and opera on video.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Contemporary Music
courses.description: This course offers opportunities to prepare oneself for experiences with new music (through preview lectures), hear performances (by visiting or faculty artists), to discuss each event informally with a faculty panel: an effort to foster informed listening to the new in music.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Popular Music
courses.description: A course on popular music from different time periods, covered through lectures, films, and listening sessions. Topics vary from year to year. May be taken for credit twice.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Hip-Hop
courses.description: This class presents a broad chronological overview of the development of hip-hop as a musical form from the late 1970s through today. It examines the development of the style in relation to direct context and to earlier African American musical and cultural forms and considers the technological and legal issues that have impacted its development. The class is listening intensive and students will be expected to know and recognize essential structures and production techniques.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Instrumental/Vocal Instruction
courses.description: Individual instruction on intermediate level in instrumental technique and repertory. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Vocal Instruction
courses.description: Individual instruction on intermediate level in vocal technique and repertory. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course and in MUS 32VM. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Vocal Master Class
courses.description: All students enrolled in voice lessons (32V, 132V, or 132C) perform for one another and their instructors. Students critique in-class performances, with emphasis on presentation, diction, dramatic effect, vocal quality, and musicality.
courses.prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in MUS 32V, 132V, or 132C.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Department Seminar
courses.description: The department seminar serves both as a general department meeting and as a forum for the presentation of research and performances by visitors, faculty, and students. Required of all undergraduate music and music humanities majors every quarter a student is a declared music major. Four units or four quarters of enrollment are required of all undergraduate ICAM music majors who choose the MUS 43. Department Seminar option for their Visitor Series requirement. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit twelve times.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Theory and Practice I
courses.description: Study of modal counterpart in the style of the sixteenth century. Two-voice species counterpoint studies. Analysis of music of the period. Musicianship studies: sight-singing, dictation, and keyboard skills.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 2C and 2CK.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Composition I
courses.description: First part in composition course sequence. Individual projects will be reviewed in seminar. Techniques of instrumentation will be developed through examination of scores and creative application. Assignments will include short exercises and analysis, and final project for standard ensemble.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 33C.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Honors Seminar in Composition
courses.description: Advanced individual projects for senior music majors pursuing honors in composition. Projects will be critically reviewed in seminar with fellow students and faculty composers.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 103A-B-C and admission into the Department of Music Honors Program in composition. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Critical Studies Seminar
courses.description: This seminar explores the history of music in relation to critical issues, such as race, gender, sexuality, the environment, and politics. Readings include recent literature in cultural studies, musicology, and sociology. Topics vary. May be taken for credit twice.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Restricted to music majors or consent of instructor; department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Topics/World Music Traditions
courses.description: A study of particular regional music in their repertory, cultural context, and interaction with other traditions. Topics vary. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Topics in Classic, Romantic, and Modern Music
courses.description: This course will focus on topics in Western music from 1750 to the early twentieth century. May be taken for credit five times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor. Department approval required. MUS 4, 8–10, or 120 recommended.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: History of Music in Western Culture I
courses.description: This sequence introduces key concepts, histories, and practices in contemporary music studies. Students will explore methodological approaches and learn about current research through focused historical and ethnographic case studies.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 1C or 2C or passing grade on proficiency exam. Music majors are recommended to take MUS 101A concurrently. Department approval required for nonmajors.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Discover Jazz
courses.description: Offers an introduction to jazz, including important performers and their associated styles and techniques. Explores the often-provocative role jazz has played in American and global society, the diverse perceptions and arguments that have surrounded its production and reception, and how these have been inflected by issues of race, class, gender, and sexuality. Specific topics vary from year to year. (Cross-listed with ETHN 179.)
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Chamber Music Performance
courses.description: Instruction in the preparation of small group performances of representative instrumental and vocal chamber music literature. May be taken for credit six times, after which students must enroll for zero units.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor through audition. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Improvisation Performance
courses.description: Master class instruction in advanced improvisation performance for declared majors and minors only or consent of instructor. Audition required at first class meeting. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor through audition. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Music Performance
courses.description: Individual or master class instruction in advanced instrumental performance. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Recital Preparation
courses.description: Advanced instrumental/vocal preparation for senior music majors pursuing honors in performance. Repertoire for a solo recital will be developed under the direction of the appropriate instrumental/vocal faculty member. Special audition required during Welcome Week preceding fall quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: by audition only; MUS 132. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Vocal Instruction
courses.description: Individual instruction in advanced vocal performance. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course and in the Vocal Master Class, MUS 32VM. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Symphonic Orchestra
courses.description: Repertoire is drawn from the classic symphonic literature of the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth centuries with a strong emphasis on recently composed and new music. Distinguished soloists, as well as The La Jolla Symphony Chorus, frequently appear with the orchestra. The La Jolla Symphony Orchestra performs two full-length programs each quarter, each program being performed twice. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Jazz Theory and Improvisation
courses.description: Study of jazz theory and improvisation, focused on fundamental rhythmic, harmonic, melodic, and formal aspects of modern jazz style. Application of theoretical knowledge to instruments and concepts will be reinforced through listening, transcription work, and composition and improvisation exercises. First course of a yearlong sequence.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 2A-B-C, proficiency exam, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Jazz Studies I
courses.description: Advanced individual projects for senior music majors pursuing honors in jazz and music of the African diaspora. Projects will be critically reviewed in seminar with fellow students and jazz faculty. First course of a yearlong sequence.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 137A-B-C and admission into the Music Department Honors Program in jazz. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Department Seminar
courses.description: The department seminar serves both as a general department meeting and as a forum for the presentation of research and performances by visitors, faculty, and students. Required of all undergraduate music majors every quarter.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Art of Sound
courses.description: Survey of applications of audio technology to music and related art forms. Physical and perceptual properties of sound and its artistic uses.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 1A, 2A, 5, 6, or 7, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Audio/MlDI Studio Techniques I
courses.description: First class in a yearlong sequence. Surveys hardware and software resources in an advanced analog/digital and media studio. Required course for use of the studio. Topics include: electronic and computer music, digital and analog audio signal mixing and manipulation, studio devices, interfacing, compositional applications, MIDI synchronization, performance and student projects. 174A focuses on signals, mics, device-based recording, mixing, monitoring.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 170; restricted to music, ICAM-music, and ICAM-visual arts majors and minors, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Musical Psychoacoustics
courses.description: Survey of psychoacoustical phenomena, theories of hearing, and their relation to musical perception and cognition. Techniques of psychoacoustical experimentation.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 170 recommended; restricted to music, ICAM-music, and ICAM-visual arts majors and minors, or consent of instructor. Depending on the instructor, this course may include the following tools: MATLAB.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Technology Seminar
courses.description: Selected topics in music technology and its application to composition and/or performance. Offerings vary according to faculty availability and interest. May be taken for credit twice. Department approval required.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor, MUS 171 recommended.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent reading, research, or creative work under the direction of a faculty member, provided no course covering the material to be studied already exists, and the study area derives from previous course work.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and department chair approval. Department approval required. Pass/Not Pass grade only. May be taken for credit twice.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Projects in New Music Performance
courses.description: Performance of contemporary music. Different sections represent active performance ensembles. A core requirement for music graduate students as outlined in the curriculum.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Projects in New Music Performance
courses.description: Performance of contemporary music. Different sections represent active performance ensembles. A core requirement for music graduate students as outlined in the curriculum.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Projects in New Music Performance
courses.description: Performance of contemporary music. Different sections represent active performance ensembles. A core requirement for music graduate students as outlined in the curriculum.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Projects in New Music Performance
courses.description: Performance of contemporary music. Different sections represent active performance ensembles. A core requirement for music graduate students as outlined in the curriculum.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Projects in Composition
courses.description: Meetings on group basis with faculty composer in sessions devoted to the study of composition.
courses.prerequisites_text: 203A-B-C and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Focus on Composition
courses.description: The purpose of this seminar is to bring in the entire population of the graduate composition program (all students and faculty) for in-depth discussion of critical issues in music theory and composition. Each meeting will feature a formal presentation by either a student, faculty member, or visitor, followed by lively and challenging debate on relevant issues.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Experimental Studies Seminar
courses.description: Seminars growing out of current faculty interests. The approach tends to be speculative and includes individual projects or papers as well as assigned readings. In the past, such areas as new instrumental and vocal resources, mixed media, and compositional linguistics have been offered.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in music; others by written consent of instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Integrative Studies I
courses.description: Seminar discussions and individual meetings devoted to the interdisciplinary study of music, sound, and society. Students are introduced to key ideas, important thinkers, and influential practitioners in an array of related fields, and are invited to explore the intersecting roles of culture, cognition, and creativity, and how musical behaviors and phenomena relate to matters of ideology, nationality, ethnicity, social class, race, and gender.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Music Performance
courses.description: Individual or master class instruction in advanced instrumental/vocal performance.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor through audition.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Symphonic Orchestra
courses.description: Repertoire is drawn from the classic symphonic literature of the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth centuries with a strong emphasis on recently composed and new music. Distinguished soloists, as well as The La Jolla Symphony Chorus, frequently appear with the orchestra. The La Jolla Symphony Orchestra performs two full-length programs each quarter, each program being performed twice. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Focus on Performance
courses.description: The purpose of this seminar is to bring together performance students, faculty, and guests for discussion, presentation of student and faculty projects, performances by guest artists, and master classes with different members of the performance faculty.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor. (S/U grade option only.)

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Projects in Computer Music
courses.description: Meetings on group basis with computer music faculty in support of individual student research projects.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and completion of MUS 270A-B-C.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research. (S/U grades permitted.) May be repeated for credit. Enrollment by consent of instructor only.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Research Projects and Independent Study
courses.description: Individual research projects relevant to the student’s selected area of graduate interest conducted in continuing relationship with a faculty adviser in preparation of the master’s thesis or doctoral dissertation.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in music; others by written consent of instructor and department approval. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: Participation in the undergraduate teaching program is required of all graduate students at the equivalent of twenty-five percent time for three quarters (six units is required for all graduate students).
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in music; others by written consent of instructor and department approval. (S/U grade option only.)

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Experience NanoEngineering
courses.description: Introduction to NanoEngineering lab-based skills. Hands-on training and experimentation with nanofabrication techniques, integration, and analytical tools. This class is for NANO majors who are incoming first-year students, to be taken their first year. P/NP grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Engineering Computation Using MATLAB Online
courses.description: Introduction to solution of engineering problems using computational methods. Formulating problem statements, selecting algorithms, writing computer programs, and analyzing output using MATLAB. Computational problems from NanoEngineering, chemical engineering, and materials science are introduced. This is a fully online, self-paced course that utilizes multi-platform instructional techniques (video, text, and instructional coding environments). The course requires no prior programming skills. Cross-listed with CENG 15R. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: NANO 15, NANO 15R, CENG 15, or CENG 15R.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Introduction to Nanomaterials Synthesis Lab
courses.description: Lab-based course to introduce the chemical synthesis of nanomaterials. Hands-on training in chemical synthesis and basic characterization tools. Program or materials fees may apply.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Foundations in NanoEngineering: Chemical Principles
courses.description: Chemical and biochemical principles tailored to nanotechnologies. Chemical interactions, classical and statistical thermodynamics of small systems, diffusion, carbon-based nanomaterials, supramolecular chemistry, colloid and polymer chemistry, lipid vesicles, surface functionalization, catalysis, biomolecular interactions, and signal pathways. Priority enrollment given to NanoEngineering majors. Prerequisites : CHEM 6C. Restricted to NanoEngineering majors or by department approval.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Electronic Devices and Circuits for NanoEngineers
courses.description: Overview of electrical devices and CMOS integrated circuits emphasizing fabrication processes, and scaling behavior. Design, and simulation of submicron CMOS circuits including amplifiers active filters digital logic, and memory circuits. Limitations of current technologies and possible impact of nanoelectronic technologies.
courses.prerequisites_text: NANO 15, NANO 11, MATH 20B or MATH 20D, and PHYS 2B.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: NanoEngineering System Design Seminar
courses.description: Seminar series focused on strategies in system design and solving engineering problems.
courses.prerequisites_text: NANO 115L.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Thermodynamics of Materials
courses.description: Fundamental laws of thermodynamics for simple substances; application to flow processes and to nonreacting mixtures; statistical thermodynamics of ideal gases and crystalline solids; chemical and materials thermodynamics; multiphase and multicomponent equilibria in reacting systems; electrochemistry.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Research project as equivalent to a “senior thesis” can be approved for two NanoEngineering elective courses (eight units total). This course is taken as an elective on a P/NP basis. It must be done in consecutive quarters and the student must find a faculty member who will oversee the research project. Eligible students must have completed at least ninety units and must have a UC San Diego cumulative GPA of 3.0 or better. Detailed policy and procedures may be obtained from the Student Affairs Office.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Graduate Seminar in Chemical and Nano Engineering
courses.description: Each graduate student in chemical or nano engineering is expected to attend a weekly seminar dealing with current topics in nano and chemical engineering. Topics will vary. Cross-listed with CENG 205. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit up to four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Introduction to NanoEngineering
courses.description: Understanding nanotechnology, broad implications, miniaturization: scaling laws; nanoscale physics; types and properties of nanomaterials; nanomechanical oscillators, nano(bio)electronics, nanoscale heat transfer; fluids at the nanoscale; machinery cell; applications of nanotechnology and nanobiotechnology. Students may not receive credit for both NANO 201 and CENG 211.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Intermolecular and Surface Forces
courses.description: Development of quantitative understanding of the different intermolecular forces between atoms and molecules and how these forces give rise to interesting phenomena at the nanoscale, such as flocculation, wetting, self-assembly in biological (natural) and synthetic systems. Cross-listed with CENG 212. Students may not receive credit for both NANO 202 and CENG 212.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Structure and Analysis of Solids
courses.description: Key concepts in the atomic structure and bonding of solids such as metals, ceramics, and semiconductors. Symmetry operations, point groups, lattice types, space groups, simple and complex inorganic compounds, structure/property comparisons, structure determination with X-ray diffraction. Ionic, covalent, metallic bonding compared with physical properties. Atomic and molecular orbitals, bands verses bonds, free electron theory. Cross-listed with MATS 227, MAE 251 and CHEM 222. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: CHEM 222, MAE 251, MATS 227, or NANO 227.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing .

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Advanced BioPhotonics
courses.description: Basic physics and chemistry of interaction of photons with matter; photonic radiation pressure; advanced optoelectronic detection systems, devices, methods, time-resolved fluorescent, chemiluminescent methods, fluorescent energy transfer techniques, quantum dots, near-field optical techniques, mechanisms of light sensitive biological systems including chloroplasts for photosynthetic energy conversion and basis of vision processes. Cross-listed with BENG 247A and ECE 247A.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Polymer Science and Engineering
courses.description: Quantitative basic understanding of different branches of polymer science varying from polymer chemistry, characterization, thermodynamics, rheological properties, smart materials, self-assembly in biopolymers (natural) and synthetic polymers, and applications of polymers ranging from medicine to structure. Cross-listed with MATS 257/BENG 242/MAE 257. Students may receive credit for one of the following: NANO 257, MATS 257, BENG 242, or MAE 257.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Thermodynamics of Solids
courses.description: The thermodynamics and statistical mechanics of solids. Basic concepts, equilibrium properties of alloy systems, thermodynamic information from phase diagrams, surfaces and interfaces, crystalline defects. Cross-listed with MATS 201A, MAE 271A, and ECE 238A. Students may receive credit for one of the following: NANO 265, MATS 201A, MAE 271A, ECE 238A.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Graduate Research in NanoEngineering
courses.description: Graduate research in NanoEngineering. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit four times for a maximum of twelve units. Prerequisites : consent of instructor and graduate standing.

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Neurology General Clinical Selective Clerkship
courses.description: Provides opportunities for practical application of neurological skills to the understanding and treatment of a variety of clinical disorders of the nervous system.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of first two years of medical school. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Subintern Pediatric Neurology
courses.description: Subinterns are responsible for the primary care of hospitalized pediatric neurology patients under direct resident and attending physician supervision. Students will perform procedures such as lumbar puncture and participate in night call, daily teaching round, neurology grand rounds, and journal clubs.
courses.prerequisites_text: Neurology 401 or consent of instructor. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Neurology Outpatient
courses.description: The student will rotate through the general and subspecialty (stroke, epilepsy, headache, nerve, and muscle) neurology clinics based at UC San Diego Medical Center, Perlman, VAMC, and Children’s Hospital. There are lectures and clinical conferences.
courses.prerequisites_text: Neurosciences 401 or equivalent. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Clinical Independent Study
courses.description: Independent clinical study for medical students (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Neurosciences
courses.description: Specialized advanced topic areas in neurosciences will be addressed in an interactive seminar course format. A different specific topic will be considered each quarter as announced in advance. Students will each present an aspect of the topic area and participate in discussions.
courses.prerequisites_text: priority given to neuroscience PhD students, or consent of instructor. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Mechanisms of Pain
courses.description: Anatomical and pharmacological substrates activated following tissue or nerve injury will be discussed. Changes in afferents and spinal cord, including increased expressions of channels and receptors during chronic pain states will be emphasized. Clinical relevance and treatment will be included. (S/U grades only.) (F)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Neurosciences Research
courses.description: Independent study. (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Apprenticeship Teaching
courses.description: Participation in the department teaching program is required of all students working toward a PhD. In general, students are not expected to teach in the first year but are required to serve as teaching assistants or tutors for one quarter at any time during their subsequent years of training. The amount of teaching required is equivalent to the duties expected of a 50 percent assistant for one quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: neurosciences graduate students. (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Professional Practice II
courses.description: The second in a series of four lecture-based courses dedicated to defining professionalism for healthcare providers. Lectures, readings, and discussion topics focused on patient- and family-centered care, understanding patients as people, working in interdisciplinary teams, and responding to adverse events.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75).

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Medicine I
courses.description: The first in a series of four lecture-based courses studying the clinical presentation, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of patients seeking care for common medical conditions in primary and specialty care settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 214.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Pharmacology and Pharmacotherapeutics I
courses.description: The first in a series of four lecture-based courses that explores the knowledge and concepts required to safely prescribe and monitor medications used to diagnose and treat common medical conditions in primary care and emergency department settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 214.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Human Physiology and Pathophysiology II
courses.description: This is the second in a series of two lecture-based courses that offers a comprehensive overview of normal human organ function, alterations in normal function, and the interaction of organ systems in states of health and disease.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 214.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Patient Education
courses.description: This course explores the effects of health literacy, patient education, and shared decision-making on patient care outcomes. Lab sessions will utilize clinical scenarios, case studies, and simulations that allow learners to practice new skills.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75).

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Reasoning I
courses.description: The first in a series of four lecture- and lab-based courses designed to engage learners in team-based activities that require them to integrate newly acquired knowledge and skill to develop and strengthen their clinical reasoning ability.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 212, PAE 215, and PAE 216.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Diagnostic Studies I
courses.description: The first of a two-part series designed to provide learners with an overview of common medical lab science assays utilized for the purposes of patient evaluation, diagnosis, and monitoring. Assay selection, interpretation, and value-based care concepts are emphasized.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75).

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics courses are reserved for learners who require extra time to complete the clinical phase of training due to factors such as hardship, leave of absence, remediation, or deceleration. Credit hours vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and departmental approval required.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Family Medicine Rotation
courses.description: This supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the clinical evaluation and management of patients seeking preventive, urgent, acute, and chronic care in a primary care setting. Encounters will include experience with infants, children, adolescents, adults, and elderly.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Internal Medicine Rotation
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the comprehensive, longitudinal care of adult patients in an internal medicine specialty.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Pediatric Rotation
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the care of patients in the primary care specialty of pediatrics which focuses on the care of patients from birth to adolescence through young adulthood.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Women’s Health Rotation
courses.description: This supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the clinical evaluation and management of patients seeking women’s health, to include prenatal and gynecologic care. Encounters will include adolescents, adults, and elderly.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Mental and Behavioral Health Rotation
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the care of patients seeking behavioral and mental healthcare across the lifespan. Learners will participate in the evaluation and management of patients with mental and behavioral health concerns.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Surgery Rotation
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the care of patients in a surgical specialty. Emphasis will include a focus on the physician assistant’s role as a member of the surgical management team.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Emergency Medicine Rotation
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the care of patients in an emergency department setting with a focus on the evaluation and management of patients who present with acute, traumatic, urgent, and emergent medical needs.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Elective Rotation I
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in a medical or surgical discipline. Learners will elect additional experiences in a specialty of their choice in settings that include inpatient, outpatient, surgery, urgent care, and the emergency department.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Elective Rotation II
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in a medical or surgical discipline. Learners will elect additional experiences in a specialty of their choice in settings that include inpatient, outpatient, surgery, urgent care, and the emergency department.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Elective Rotation III
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in a medical or surgical discipline. Learners will elect additional experiences in a specialty of their choice in settings that include inpatient, outpatient, surgery, urgent care, and the emergency department.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Independent Study for Clinical Concentrations
courses.description: This four-week non-clinical experience provides learners on a clinical concentration path with time to focus on completing their capstone project. Learners will also create a self-directed learning plan to prepare for final written and practical summative assessments required for graduation.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 410, PAE 411, PAE 412, PAE 420, PAE 430, PAE 440, and PAE 450.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Capstone
courses.description: The first of four one-week seminars designed to augment supervised clinical practice experiences wherein learners will apply the knowledge, skills, and attitudes acquired throughout the MAS-PAS program of study. A letter grade for each seminar will be assigned upon completion of seminar IV (PAE 494).
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Public Health
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the infrastructure of public health; the analytical tools employed by public health practitioners; bio-psychosocial perspectives of public health problems; health promotion/disease prevention; quality assessment in public health; and legal and ethical concerns. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 40. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 40 and PH 40.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Methods and Ethics in Public Health Research
courses.description: This course will lay a foundation for understanding how to conduct research to answer questions about public health. It aims to teach students why research is done the way it is, what questions we can and can’t answer, and the methodological and ethical limits that must be considered along the way. Students will learn to think critically about the implications and limitations of existing research, and to form their own research questions about public health and the ways to investigate answers.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Primary Care and Public Health
courses.description: This course explores historical and current interactions, achievements, and challenges of primary care and public health. It will analyze the impact of common medical conditions such as obesity, diabetes, mental health disorders, and others on individuals, their families, and society. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 50. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 50 and PH 50.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Exploring Public Health
courses.description: This seminar-style course offers students the opportunity to explore key areas of public health, covering foundational principles across a variety of topics. Subjects range and may include, but are not limited to, career pathways in public health, strategies for maintaining well-being and academic success, mental health awareness and support, sexual health and reproductive rights, mindfulness practices, financial wellness, stress management, and more.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Selected topics in the field of public health.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Epidemiology
courses.description: This course covers the basic principles of epidemiology, with applications to investigations of noninfectious (“chronic”) and infectious diseases. Explores various study designs appropriate for disease surveillance and studies of etiology and prevention. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 101. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 101 and PH 101.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PSYC 60, HDS 60, MATH 11, or COGS 14B, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Biostatistics in Public Health
courses.description: Fundamentals of biostatistics and basic methods for analysis of continuous and binary outcomes for one, two, or several groups. Includes: summarizing and displaying data; probability; statistical distributions; central limit theorem, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing; comparing means of continuous variables between two groups; comparing proportions between two groups; simple and multiple linear regression. Hands-on data analysis using software and statistical applications in public health. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 102. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 102 and PH 102.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PSYC 60, HDS 60, MATH 11, or COGS 14B, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Health Behavior and Chronic Diseases
courses.description: This course introduces health behavior concepts through applications to chronic disease prevention. The focus is on smoking, dietary behaviors, and physical activity and is organized around relationships to health, measurement, influencing factors, interventions, and translation to public health practice. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 110. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 110 and PH 110.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Environmental and Occupational Health
courses.description: This core public health course addresses the fundamentals of environmental and occupational health, including identification of hazards, basic toxicology, risk assessment, prevention/protection, and regulatory/control policies. Specific environmental and occupational hazards and relevant case studies will be presented. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 130. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 130 and PH 130.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 101 or FMPH 101, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Clinical Nutrition in Public Health
courses.description: Clinical nutrition is the study of nutrition and diet as related to the prevention and treatment of human disease. The practical and psychosocial aspects of diet modification and food/food product availability are key aspects of clinical nutrition practice, whether individual or community based, irrespective of whether the goal is primary prevention or disease treatment. Students will identify applications and translation of nutritional guidelines and recommendations into behavior in the course. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing. Renumbered from FMPH 161. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 161 and PH 161.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Selected topics in the field of public health. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Additional prerequisites may be required at instructor’s discretion. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing. Department approval required. Renumbered from FMPH 191.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Capstone I
courses.description: This is the first of a two-part capstone series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students will integrate the skills and knowledge gained throughout the BSPH program and learn critical elements of public health research and practice. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, and PH 120 or FMPH 120. Department approval required. Restricted to senior public health majors only. Renumbered from FMPH 193. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: PH 193, PH 193R, or FMPH 193.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Pedagogy and Learning Apprenticeship
courses.description: Under the supervision of an instructor, undergraduate students gain teaching experience through practical experiences in course management and effective teaching methods. May be taken for credit up to two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: a minimum of A– in the course in which the student plans to assist, a 3.0 cumulative UC GPA, and instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Investigation of public health topics through directed reading and discussion by a small group of students. Opportunities can also include experiential and research components. Study must be under supervision of a faculty member and approval must be secured from the faculty member prior to registering. P/NP grades only. Renumbered from FMPH 198. PH 198 and/or FMPH 198 may be taken for credit a combined total of nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual undergraduate study or research not covered by the present course offerings. Study or research must be under the direction of a faculty member in the Department of Family Medicine and Public Health and approval must be secured from the faculty member prior to registering. P/NP grades only. Renumbered from FMPH 199. PH 199 and/or FMPH 199 may be taken for credit a combined total of nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Foundations of Public Health
courses.description: This course provides students with an overview of the foundations of public health. It is organized into three modules: 1) science of public health (history, philosophy, core functions, causes of morbidity and mortality, and prevention), 2) factors related to human health (environmental, biological, genetic, behavioral, psychological, cultural, social, political, global, and ecological), and 3) public health leadership (leadership, management, negotiation, mediation, and interprofessional connections).

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: JDP Public Health Seminar
courses.description: This course combines didactic instruction, interactive sessions, and student presentations. Topics cover study design, ethics, data analysis and management techniques, and qualitative research will be presented.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Epidemiology Practicum
courses.description: Students will explore an epidemiologic research question by reviewing relevant published literature, and then design and conduct appropriate data analysis using a preexisting dataset.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Cultural Perceptions about Health and Disease
courses.description: This course takes an interdisciplinary look at the relationship between culture and health in diverse sociostructural contexts.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: HSRIS Colloquium Series
courses.description: The HSRIS colloquium series is a program of empirical research seminars focused on the most important issues facing patients, providers, health care systems, and policymakers today. It provides an opportunity for HSRIS doctoral students across all stages of completion to meet regularly, analyze and critique ongoing research, and participate in stimulating discussion with HSRIS faculty and guest lecturers.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Practicum in Global Health and Health Behavior
courses.description: Students will learn about grant writing, project management, preparation of manuscripts for publication and presentations for scientific meetings, and also work individually with a faculty mentor in preparing manuscripts using data from a specific health behavior intervention.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Dissemination and Implementation Science in Health: An Introduction
courses.description: This course will emphasize the unique aspects of dissemination and implementation research, including the types of questions it seeks to answer, the outcomes examined and how they differ from other types of studies, the models and frameworks commonly used, and the qualitative and quantitative methods employed.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Topics of special interest in public health. Topics may vary from quarter to quarter.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study in Public Health
courses.description: Individual graduate study or research not covered by present course offerings. Study or research must be under the direction of a faculty member in the School of Public Health and approval must be secured from the faculty member and track director prior to registering.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Dissertation Research in Public Health
courses.description: Public health doctoral program dissertation research units.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Biostatistics
courses.description: Students will understand principles of measurement of clinical data, recognize data types, and determine statistical methods for analysis of a given dataset. They will gain experience in preparing a clinical dataset for analysis. Students will learn basic data visualization, statistical testing and inference, and statistical modeling with R.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 400. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 400 and PH 400.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Epidemiology
courses.description: This course provides a foundational understanding of principles and methods used to study the distribution and determinants of health and disease in populations. Topics include study design, data collection, measures of disease frequency, and risk assessment. Through lectures and small group discussions, students learn to critically evaluate epidemiological research, understand the ethical considerations in conducting epidemiological studies, and recognize common sources of bias and confounding.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 401. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 401 and PH 401.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Cardiovascular Disease Epidemiology
courses.description: This is an MPH-level course designed to introduce topics in cardiovascular disease epidemiology using the following definition of epidemiology as a guide: Epidemiology is the study of the distribution and determinants of health-related states or events in specified populations, and the application of this study to the control of health problems. As such, the course provides an overview of the prevalence, incidence, and key risk factors for major cardiovascular diseases.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401. Students may only receive credit for one of these courses: PH 417, PH 417R, or FMPH 417.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Mental Health Across the Life Course
courses.description: This course examines mental health from infancy through childhood into adulthood and aging. Students will learn how perturbations in mental health manifest differently at different developmental stages over the life course. The course will also cover how early life exposures to stressful circumstances can lead to symptoms, disorder, or disease and how these manifest themselves across development. Students will explore potential strategies for identification of risk, prevention, and intervention.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB89) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 427. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 427 and PH 427.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Substance Use and Population Health
courses.description: This course offers a window into the patterns, drivers, and consequences of substance use from a public health perspective. It also introduces various prevention, treatment, and harm reduction approaches. Through assessment of current epidemiologic data, application of conceptual frameworks, engagement with researchers and practitioners, and reflection on prevention, treatment, and harm reduction policies and strategies, we will explore the complexity of substance use and population health.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, and PB89). Students cannot receive credit for PH 429 if they have already completed FMPH 491 subtitled “Substance Use and Population Health.”

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: The Organization and Financing of the U.S. Health-Care System
courses.description: Students will learn about the organization and financing of health services in the United States and the implications of system characteristics for quality, equity, and health-care costs; develop an understanding of how health policy decisions are made in the United States; and learn how health-care financing in the US compares with other countries around the world. Students will develop the background and skills to solve a range of problems in the fields of health policy and public health.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB88) and successfully completed FMPH 405 or PH 405. Renumbered from FMPH 441. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 441 and PH 441.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Qualitative Research Methods
courses.description: This course introduces master’s students to qualitative research methods, emphasizing the strategies and applications of this methodology in public health, health justice, and community-engaged research. Through lectures, group work, interactive sessions, and practical exercises, students will gain foundational knowledge and skills in qualitative research. Topics also include theoretical foundations of research, biocultural ethics, and the advantages of numerous qualitative inquiry techniques.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB88). Students cannot receive credit for PH 442 if they have already completed FMPH 491 subtitled “Qualitative Research Methods.”

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Course will cover various topics in the field of public health. May be taken for credit up to twelve times for a maximum of forty-eight units.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 491.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: MPH Practicum Field Placement
courses.description: This course provides MPH students the opportunity to participate in a short-term, field-based public health or population-based experience. Students will engage in a field experience in collaboration with a sponsoring organization and qualified site mentor. Students are expected to apply theory, skills, and training acquired through the public health course work within a real-life setting. Students will develop written and oral communication skills that employ public health concepts and methods.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91). Renumbered from FMPH 496B. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 496B and PH 496B.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study under the guidance of a Wertheim School of Public Health faculty member. May be taken for credit up to twelve times for a maximum of forty-eight units.
courses.prerequisites_text: program approval required.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Master’s Capstone/Thesis
courses.description: Students complete their capstone/thesis, and potentially submit their capstone/thesis for publication and/or present their capstone/thesis to stakeholders. May be taken for credit up to six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistical Methods I
courses.description: Introductory graduate course on applied statistical data analysis, focusing on multiple linear regression and using the R statistical software. The course addresses issues related to model interpretation, model assumptions, confounding, interactions, testing of coefficients and ANOVA, adjusting for multiple comparisons, heteroscedasticity, model diagnostics, variable selection, prediction error, cross-validation, and resampling via the bootstrap. Renumbered from FMPH 221. Students may not receive credit for PHB 221 and FMPH 221. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the biostatistics degree requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: biostatistics major or program approval.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistical Methods in Clinical Trials
courses.description: The graduate-level course will cover statistical aspects of clinical trial design, monitoring, analysis, and ethics of human subjects research. Design and computations will be emphasized. Renumbered from FMPH 224. Students may not receive credit for PHB 224 and FMPH 224. Must be taken for a letter grade if applied to biostatistics degree requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 221 and FMPH 222 or PHB 222 and FMPH 223 or PHB 223 or program approval. Restricted to PB76, PB77, PB79, PB80, PB81, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Statistical Learning and Multivariate Analysis
courses.description: This graduate course introduces concepts, methods, and applications of statistical learning and multivariate data analysis, including prediction, classification, regularization, decision trees, principal components analysis, and clustering. Data analysis will be emphasized. Renumbered from FMPH 227. Students may not receive credit for PHB 227 and FMPH 227. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the biostatistics degree requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 221 and FMPH 222 or PHB 222 or program approval.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistics Rotation
courses.description: This practicum provides hand-on experience with biomedical research and data analysis. Working within a specific biomedical domain (e.g., cancer, genomics, or physical activity research), students will conduct original data analysis and prepare or substantially contribute to a final project report. Renumbered from FMPH 241. PHB 241 and/or FMPH 241 may be taken for credit for a combined total of five times.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 221 and FMPH 222 or PHB 222; biostatistics major only.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Practicum in Biostatistics A
courses.description: This is the first in a sequence of two core courses for the MS degree in biostatistics. The course takes advantage of the extensive involvement of the program faculty in collaborative and interdisciplinary work within the life sciences. Didactic instruction on best practices in statistical collaboration. Under supervision, the students will participate in applied, real-life projects stemming from the research and collaborations of the faculty in the Division of Biostatistics.
