Renumbered from FMPH 243A. Students may not receive credit for PHB 243A and FMPH 243A.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 222 and FMPH 223 or PHB 223. Restricted to major code PB76.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Foundations in Biostatistics A
courses.description: This course will mainly focus on probability theory and mathematical statistics, which are essential building blocks for more advanced inference tools. Topics include probability theory, (multivariate) random variables, functions of random variables, expectations, variance and moments, common families of distributions, properties of a random sample, statistics and sampling distribution, convergence of a sequence of random variables. Renumbered from FMPH 244A. Students may not receive credit for PHB 244A and FMPH 244A. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the biostatistics degree requirements. Restricted to major code PB76.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistics Journal Club
courses.description: This is a biweekly, structured journal club. Students will critically read assigned articles. During meetings, students work in groups to discuss specific questions regarding the assigned article, and are asked to present their answers to the class. Renumbered from FMPH 290. PHB 280 and/or FMPH 290 may be taken for credit for a combined total of six times. Restricted to major codes PB76 or PB77.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistics Seminar Series
courses.description: Through a combination of in-person and virtual seminars on Zoom, students will gain insight into current research projects presented by invited speakers. Additionally, students are provided with the opportunity to participate in lunch discussions and one-on-one meetings. All MS students in biostatistics, and biostatistics PhD students in their third year and above are highly encouraged to enroll quarterly (except for summer). May be taken for credit up to twelve times.
courses.prerequisites_text: FMPH 290 or PHB 280. Restricted to PB76 and PB77 majors.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Independent study for biostatistics graduate students in the Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science. Study of special topics for graduate students under the direction of a faculty member. Exact subject matter to be arranged in individual cases. Restricted to PB76 and PB77 majors. May be taken for credit up to twenty-one times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.description: Dissertation research for students who are advancing or have advanced to candidacy. May be taken for credit up to twelve times. Renumbered from FMPH 299. PHB 299 and/or FMPH 299 may be taken for credit for a combined total of twelve times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: A general introduction to some of the fundamental questions, texts, and methods of philosophy. Multiple topics will be covered, and may include the existence of God, the nature of mind and body, free will, ethics and political philosophy, knowledge and skepticism. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Logic
courses.description: Basic concepts and techniques in both informal and formal logic and reasoning, including a discussion of argument, inference, proof, and common fallacies, and an introduction to the syntax, semantics, and proof method in sentential (propositional) logic. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy: Ethics
courses.description: An inquiry into the nature of morality and its role in personal or social life by way of classical and/or contemporary works in ethics. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ethics and Society
courses.description: An examination of ethical principles (e.g., utilitarianism, individual rights, etc.) and their social and political applications to contemporary issues: abortion, environmental protection, and affirmative action. Ethical principles will also be applied to moral dilemmas in government, law, business, and the professions. Warren College students must take course for a letter grade in order to satisfy the Warren College general-education requirement. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: CAT 2 and 3 or CAT 2CE and 3CE or CCE 1 and 2 or DOC 2 and 3 or HUM 1 and 2 or MCWP 40 and 50 or MCWP 40R and 50R or MMW 12 and 13 or WCWP 10A and B or SYN 1 and 2 or WARR 11A and 11B or SYN 1R and 2R.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ethics and Society II
courses.description: An examination of a single set of major contemporary social, political, or economic issues (e.g., environmental ethics, international ethics) in light of ethical and moral principles and values. Warren College students must take course for a letter grade in order to satisfy the Warren College general-education requirement. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHIL 27 or POLI 27.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy in the Americas
courses.description: An exploration of central philosophical issues as they have been taken up in the diverse philosophical traditions of the Americas, such as indigenous philosophy, Latin American philosophy, American Pragmatism, and the Civil Rights movement, among others. Topics may include ethics, social and political philosophy, colonialism, philosophy of race and gender, environmentalism, and issues in philosophy of language. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Law and Society
courses.description: A survey of philosophical issues concerning law and society, such as the rule of law, the moral limits of the law, individual rights, judicial review in a constitutional democracy, the justification of punishment, and responsibility. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Climate Ethics
courses.description: This course will address the complex moral challenge of climate change. Topics include ethical values in climate modeling; the moral psychology of climate change; individual versus structural approaches to decarbonization; global justice and the distribution of greenhouse gas emissions; the ethics of geoengineering; decolonization and the climate crisis; discounting and obligations to future generations. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: First-year Student Seminar
courses.description: The First-year Student Seminar Program is designed to provide new students with the opportunity to explore an intellectual topic with a faculty member in a small seminar setting. First-year student seminars are offered in all campus departments and undergraduate colleges, and topics vary from quarter to quarter. Enrollment is limited to fifteen to twenty students, with preference given to entering first-year students. May be repeated for credit four times with change of content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Philosophy: Ancient
courses.description: An examination of ancient Greek philosophy, focusing on major works of Plato and Aristotle. PHIL 10, PHIL 111, and PHIL 112 should be taken in order. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department stamp or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Symbolic Logic I
courses.description: The syntax, semantics, and proof-theory of first order monadic and polyadic predicate logic. In this course, we will learn how to determine whether arguments that can be represented in first order predicate logic are deductively valid, how to symbolize English arguments, the rules of a natural deduction system, how to apply those rules to determine the logical status of symbolized arguments, and how to use semantic methods for determining validity and invalidity. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHIL 10 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Language
courses.description: Examination of contemporary debates about meaning, reference, truth, and thought. Topics include descriptional theories of reference, sense and reference, compositionality, truth, theories of meaning, vagueness, metaphor, and natural and formal languages. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Mind
courses.description: Different conceptions of the nature of mind and its relation to the physical world. Topics include identity theories, functionalism, eliminative materialism, internalism and externalism, subjectivity, other minds, consciousness, self-knowledge, perception, memory, and imagination. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Emotion
courses.description: The nature, function, and value of emotion. Topics include theoretical approaches to defining (and distinguishing particular) emotions; the roles of emotions in structuring perception, cognition, and action; the rationality of emotion; morality and the emotions; emotions and mental/social well-being; and specific emotions such as fear or grief. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Biology
courses.description: Philosophical problems in the biological sciences, such as the relation between biology and the physical sciences, the status and structure of evolutionary theory, and the role of biology in the social sciences. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy and Animals
courses.description: An examination of one or more philosophical issues pertaining to animals. Topics will vary and may address animal ethics, animal minds, animals in the philosophy of science or conservation, metaphysical or epistemological questions related to animals, or the treatment of animals in a particular tradition or period in the history of philosophy. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Metaethics
courses.description: An examination of foundational questions about morality, including issues such as ethical objectivity; the relation between science and ethics; metaphysical, epistemological, and semantic issues about ethics; moral expertise; moral conflict; moral motivation; morality and practical reason; and the rational authority of morality. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Contemporary Political Philosophy
courses.description: Different perspectives on central issues in contemporary political philosophy, such as the nature of state authority and political obligation, the limits of government and individual liberty, liberalism and its critics, equality and distributive justice. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Law
courses.description: A study of issues in analytical jurisprudence such as the nature of law, the relation between law and morality, and the nature of legal interpretation and issues in normative jurisprudence such as the justification of punishment, paternalism and privacy, freedom of expression, and affirmative action. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics in Bioethics
courses.description: An in-depth exploration of an issue in bioethics. Topics will vary, and may include the ethics of genetic engineering, mental capacity and genuinely informed consent, the just distribution of health care, the ethics of geo-engineering, and the ethics of climate change and health. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Culture
courses.description: This course examines the nature of culture, its significance, and its varied meanings. Topics may include case studies of culture’s relationship to psychology, politics, media, religion, and the arts. Course may include discussion of related questions concerning culture and race, class, nationalism, sexuality, and gender. Contemporary and classical readings, drawing from philosophy, anthropology, sociology, literature, religion, and related fields. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Applied Ethics
courses.description: Intensive application of ethics through contemporary moral dilemmas focused on developing oral and presentation skills in philosophy. Students will have the opportunity to join the department’s Ethics Bowl team for an annual national competition series. May be repeated for credit eight times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy Honors
courses.description: Independent study by special arrangement with and under the supervision of a faculty member, including a proposal for the honors essay. An IP grade will be awarded at the end of this quarter; a final grade will be given for both quarters at the end of 191B.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: The Honors Essay
courses.description: Continuation of 191A: independent study by special arrangement with and under the supervision of a faculty member, leading to the completion of the honors essay. A letter grade for both 191A and 191B will be given at the end of this quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Pedagogy and Learning Apprenticeship
courses.description: Under the supervision of an instructor, undergraduate students gain teaching experience through practical experiences in course management and effective teaching methods. Pedagogy and learning apprentices must have a minimum overall grade point average of 3.0. A student may not apprentice more than once for the same course for credit or for more than one course in the same quarter. May be repeated for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Directed Individual Study
courses.description: Directed individual study by special arrangement with and under the supervision of a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.) May be repeated for credit four times with change of content and approval of instructor.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Core Course in Ethics
courses.description: An introduction to some central issues in ethical theory with emphasis on classic texts or contemporary authors. May be taken for credit three times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Colloquium in Science Studies
courses.description: A forum for the presentation and discussion of research in progress in science studies by graduate students, faculty, and visitors. Students must attend the colloquium series for their entire first and second years. May be taken for credit two times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Greek Philosophy
courses.description: A study of selected texts or topics from the history of Greek philosophy. Usually centers on works by Plato or Aristotle. May be taken for credit six times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Agency, Responsibility, and Freedom
courses.description: Contemporary debates on the nature of agency, responsibility, and freedom. May include questions about free will and determinism, intentional action, group agency, culpability, and the significance of recent scientific findings on these topics. May be taken for credit six times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Agency, Morality, and Psychology Research Group
courses.description: This course is designed for students to gain feedback from students and faculty on works in progress on the topics of agency, morality, and psychology, and on contemporary research on these topics. The course is suitable for those specializing in moral psychology, agency, ethics, and philosophy mind and psychology, and for those with special interests in the topics.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: German Philosophy Reading Group
courses.description: This course meets regularly to discuss primary or secondary literature in the area of German philosophy (including Kant, Fichte, Hegel, etc.). The reading is designed both for students doing active research in the field and for those seeking to gain some familiarity with it. Nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit twenty-one times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Phenomenology Reading Group
courses.description: This course meets biweekly with students reading and presenting material from the phenomenological literature. The course is designed both for students doing active research in phenomenology and for those seeking to gain some familiarity with that tradition. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics and Methods in Contemporary Philosophy
courses.description: Investigation of central issues in contemporary philosophy. Content varies but typically will center on a recent and important philosophical book. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Science Topics and Methods
courses.description: This course meets weekly to discuss recent books or articles in philosophy of science. The reading is designed both for students doing active research in the field and for those seeking to gain some familiarity with it. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Philosophy Research and Methods
courses.description: This course meets to discuss work in progress in the history of philosophy. Its aim is to introduce understanding of the methods and standards of research in the field through constructive criticism of each other’s work. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics and Methods in Ethics
courses.description: Weekly or biweekly meetings to discuss recent literature in ethics, broadly construed so as to include ethical theory, normative ethics, jurisprudence, and historical traditions in these fields. The course is suitable for those specializing in ethics and for those seeking some familiarity with the field. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics and Methods in Latin American Philosophy
courses.description: This course is designed for students to gain feedback from students and faculty on works in progress on Latin American philosophy. The course is suitable for those specializing in historical and contemporary philosophy in Latin America and for those with special interests in the topics.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Biology Research Group
courses.description: A research group for graduate students engaged in philosophy or history of the biological sciences. The group discusses biological, historical, and philosophical articles and books and ongoing research projects. Can be taken nine times for credit with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Physics Reading Group
courses.description: A research group for graduate students engaged in philosophy or history of the physical sciences. The group discusses physical, historical, and philosophical articles and books and ongoing research projects. Can be taken nine times for credit with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Greek Reading Group
courses.description: This group provides training in reading and translating philosophical Greek by having students prepare translations of passages and lead discussions. The group helps train graduate students preparing for Departmental Greek Exam. Can be taken nine times for credit with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Directed Independent Study
courses.description: Supervised study of individually selected philosophical topics. S/U grades permitted.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Research Topics
courses.description: Advanced individual research studies under the direction of a member of the staff. Hours of outside preparation will vary with number of units taken. May be taken for credit nine times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: S/U grades permitted.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: A course designed to satisfy the requirement that graduate students should serve as teaching assistants, either in the Department of Philosophy or in one of the writing programs offered by the various colleges. Each PhD candidate must teach the equivalent of quarter time for three academic quarters. Students are permitted to sign up as TAs for a maximum of eighteen quarters.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mechanics
courses.description: First quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course, geared toward life-science majors. Equilibrium and motion of particles in one and two dimensions in the framework of Newtonian mechanics, force laws (including gravity), energy, momentum, rotational motion, conservation laws, and fluids. Examples will be drawn from astronomy, biology, sports, and current events. PHYS 1A and 1AL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both. Students continuing to PHYS 1B/1BL will also need MATH 10B or 20B.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or 20A. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mechanics Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1A. Experiments in Mechanics. PHYS 1A and 1AL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both. Students continuing to PHYS 1B/1BL will also need MATH 10B or 20B.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or 20A. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1A and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Second quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course geared toward life-science majors. Electric fields, magnetic fields, DC and AC circuitry. PHYS 1B and 1BL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1A or 2A, and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1B. Experiments in electricity and magnetism. Program or materials fee may apply. PHYS 1B and 1BL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1A or 2A, 1AL or 2BL, and MATH 10B or 20B. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Waves, Optics, and Modern Physics
courses.description: Third quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course geared toward life-science majors. The physics of oscillations and waves, vibrating strings and sound, and the interaction of light with matter as illustrated through optics and quantum mechanics. Examples from biology, sports, medicine, and current events. PHYS 1C and 1CL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1B or 2B, and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Waves, Optics, and Modern Physics Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1C. Experiments in waves, optics, and modern physics. Program or materials fee may apply. PHYS 1C and 1CL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1B or 2B, 1BL or 2CL, and MATH 10B or 20B. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1C.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Mechanics
courses.description: A calculus-based science-engineering general physics course covering vectors, motion in one and two dimensions, Newton’s first and second laws, work and energy, conservation of energy, linear momentum, collisions, rotational kinematics, rotational dynamics, equilibrium of rigid bodies, oscillations, gravitation. Students continuing to PHYS 2B/4B will also need MATH 20B. Students will not receive credit for both PHYS 2A and PHYS 2AR.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A-B or 20A or 20B or 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 2A covering charge and matter, the electric field, Gauss’s law, electric potential, capacitors and dielectrics, current and resistance, electromotive force and circuits, the magnetic field, Ampere’s law, Faraday’s law, inductance, electromagnetic oscillations, alternating currents and Maxwell’s equations. Students continuing to PHYS 2C will also need MATH 20C or 31BH.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A and MATH 20B or 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20C or 31BH.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Fluids, Waves, Thermodynamics, and Optics
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 2B covering fluid mechanics, waves in elastic media, sound waves, temperature, heat and the first law of thermodynamics, kinetic theory of gases, entropy and the second law of thermodynamics, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, geometric optics, interference and diffraction. Students continuing to PHYS 2D will need MATH 20D.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, and MATH 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20D. Prior completion of PHYS 2B is strongly recommended.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory—Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Experiments on L-R-C circuits; oscillations, resonance and damping, measurement of magnetic fields. One hour lecture and three hours laboratory. Program or materials fee may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, and 2B or 4C. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 2C or 4D.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Relativity and Quantum Physics
courses.description: A modern physics course covering atomic view of matter, electricity and radiation, atomic models of Rutherford and Bohr, relativity, X-rays, wave and particle duality, matter waves, Schrödinger’s equation, atomic view of solids, natural radioactivity.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, 2B, and MATH 20D. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20E.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory—Modern Physics
courses.description: Experiments to be chosen from refraction, diffraction and interference of microwaves, Hall effect, thermal band gap, optical spectra, coherence of light, photoelectric effect, e/m ratio of particles, radioactive decays, and plasma physics. One hour lecture and three hours laboratory. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2BL or 2CL . Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 2D or 4E.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics for Physics Majors—Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 4B covering charge and Coulomb’s law, electric field, Gauss’s law, electric potential, capacitors and dielectrics, current and resistance, magnetic field, Ampere’s law, Faraday’s law, inductance, AC circuits.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A-B or PHYS 2A-B-C, MATH 20A-B-C or 31BH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20E or 31CH.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Energy and the Environment
courses.description: A course covering energy fundamentals, energy use in an industrial society and the impact of large-scale energy consumption. It addresses topics on fossil fuel, heat engines, solar energy, nuclear energy, energy conservation, transportation, air pollution and global effects. Concepts and quantitative analysis.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Introductory Special Topics
courses.description: From time to time a member of the regular faculty or a resident visitor will give a self-contained course on an introductory topic in their special area of research or help students prepare to succeed in the physics major. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only. May be repeated up to six times, provided the same topic is not repeated.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a topic by special arrangement with a faculty member. P/NP grading only.
courses.prerequisites_text: lower-division standing. Completion of thirty units at UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0, and a completed and approved Special Studies form. Department stamp required.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetism I
courses.description: Coulomb’s law, electric fields, electrostatics; conductors and dielectrics; steady currents, elements of circuit theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A-B-C-D; MATH 20A, 20B, 20C or 31BH, 20D, 20E or 31CH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mechanics I
courses.description: Phase flows, bifurcations, linear oscillations, calculus of variations, Lagrangian dynamics, conservation laws, central forces, systems of particles, collisions, coupled oscillations.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A-B-C-D, MATH 20A-B-C or 31BH, 20D, 20E or 31CH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Experimental Techniques
courses.description: Laboratory-lecture course covering practical techniques used in research laboratories. Possible topics include computer interfacing of instruments, sensors, and actuators; programming for data acquisition/analysis; electronics; measurement techniques; mechanical design/machining; mechanics of materials; thermal design/control; vacuum/cryogenic techniques; optics; particle detection. PHYS 122 was formerly numbered PHYS 121. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 120.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Physics II
courses.description: Matrix mechanics, angular momentum, spin, and the two-state system. Approximation methods and the hydrogen spectrum. Identical particles, atomic and nuclear structures. Scattering theory. Three hours lecture, one-hour discussion session.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 100B and 130A. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter/Materials Science Laboratory
courses.description: A project-oriented laboratory course utilizing state-of-the-art experimental techniques in materials science. The course prepares students for research in a modern condensed matter-materials science laboratory. Under supervision, the students develop their own experimental ideas after investigating current research literature. With the use of sophisticated state-of-the-art instrumentation students conduct research, write a research paper, and make verbal presentations. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2CL and 2DL. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Special Topics
courses.description: From time to time a member of the regular faculty or a resident visitor will give a self-contained short course on a topic in his or her special area of research. This course is not offered on a regular basis, but it is estimated that it will be given once each academic year. Course may be taken for credit up to two times as topics vary (the course subtitle will be different for each distinct topic). Students who repeat the same topic in PHYS 139 will have the duplicate credit removed from their academic record.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A-B-C-D or 4A-B-C-D-E, MATH 20A-B-C or 31BH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Statistical and Thermal Physics I
courses.description: Integrated treatment of thermodynamics and statistical mechanics; statistical treatment of entropy, review of elementary probability theory, canonical distribution, partition function, free energy, phase equilibrium, introduction to ideal quantum gases.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 130A. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Computational Physics II: PDE and Matrix Models
courses.description: Project-based computational physics laboratory course for modern physics and engineering problems with student’s choice of Fortran90/95, or C/C++. Applications of finite element PDE models are chosen from quantum mechanics and nanodevices, fluid dynamics, electromagnetism, materials physics, and other modern topics.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Modern Cosmology
courses.description: An introduction to our current understanding of the universe, its history and content. The course introduces the geometry of the universe, the origin of structure, maps of the universe, and inference of cosmic parameters. Topics include big bang nucleosynthesis, the cosmic microwave background, the quantum origin of density fluctuations, dark matter, and the cosmological constant.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A-B-C-D-E.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biological Physics
courses.description: The course teaches how a few fundamental models from statistical physics provide quantitative explanatory frameworks for many seemingly unrelated problems in biology. Case studies rotate from year to year and may include ion channel gating, cooperative binding, protein-DNA interaction, gene regulation, molecular motor dynamics, cytoskeletal assembly, biological electricity, population and evolutionary dynamics. May be coscheduled with PHYS 275.
courses.prerequisites_text: CHEM 126 or 131 or 132 or the combination of PHYS 100A and 110A. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 140A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar on Physics
courses.description: Undergraduate seminars organized around the research interests of various faculty members. P/NP grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem by special arrangement with a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and departmental chair.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Honors Thesis Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Honors thesis research for seniors participating in the Honors Program. Research is conducted under the supervision of a physics faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Honors Program in Physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Theoretical Mechanics I
courses.description: Review of Lagrangian mechanics: calculus of variations, Noether’s theorem, constraints, central forces, coupled oscillations. Continuum mechanics: strings and membranes, Sturm-Liouville theory, dispersion. Hamiltonian mechanics: equations of motion, Poisson brackets, canonical transformations, Hamilton-Jacobi theory, action-angle variables, adiabatic invariants.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mathematical Methods for Physics
courses.description: An introduction to mathematical methods used in theoretical physics. Topics include a review of complex variable theory, applications of the Cauchy residue theorem, asymptotic series, method of steepest descent, Fourier and Laplace transforms, series solutions for ODE’s and related special functions, Sturm Liouville theory, variational principles, boundary value problems, and Green’s function techniques.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Estimation and Scaling in Physics
courses.description: This course stresses approximate techniques in physics, both in terms of quantitative estimation and scaling relationships. A broad range of topics may include drag, aerodynamics, fluids, waves, heat transfer, mechanics of materials, sound, optical phenomena, nuclear physics, societal-scale energy, weather and climate change, human metabolic energy. Undergraduates wishing to enroll will be expected to have prior completion of PHYS 100B, PHYS 110A, PHYS 130B, and PHYS 140A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Nonequilibrium Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Transport phenomena; kinetic theory and the Chapman-Enskog method; hydrodynamic theory; nonlinear effects and the mode coupling method. Stochastic processes; Langevin and Fokker-Planck equation; fluctuation-dissipation relation; multiplicative processes; dynamic field theory; Martin-Siggia-Rose formalism; dynamical scaling theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 210A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Solid-State Physics I
courses.description: The first of a two-quarter course in solid-state physics. Covers a range of solid-state phenomena that can be understood within an independent particle description. Topics include chemical versus band-theoretical description of solids, electronic band structure calculation, lattice dynamics, transport phenomena and electrodynamics in metals, optical properties, semiconductor physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics I
courses.description: Quantum principles of state (pure, composite, entangled, mixed), observables, time evolution, and measurement postulate. Simple soluble systems: two-state, harmonic oscillator, and spherical potentials. Angular momentum and spin. Time-independent approximations.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Fields I
courses.description: Introduction to field quantization for relativistic scalar, Fermion, and gauge fields. Symmetries and conservation laws. Calculation of cross sections and reaction rates via perturbation theory and Feynman diagram methods, including for tree-level processes in quantum electrodynamics.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 212C.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Selected Topics in Quantum Fields
courses.description: Selected additional topics in quantum field theory, varying year by year depending on the instructor. Topics may include effective field theory, anomalies, instantons, monopoles, large N methods, topological terms, coherent state path integrals, field theories of condensed matter, QFT in other space-time dimensions, conformal field theories, lattice gauge theory, strong coupling methods, RG flows and constraints, phases of QFT, supersymmetry, dualities, AdS/CFT. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 215B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Field Theory and the Renormalization Group
courses.description: Application of field theoretic and renormalization group methods to problems in condensed matter, or particle physics. Topics will vary and may include phase transition and critical phenomena; many body quantum systems; quantum chromodynamics and the electroweak model.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 210A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter/Materials Science Laboratory
courses.description: A project-oriented laboratory course utilizing state-of-the-art experimental techniques in materials science. The course prepares students for research in a modern condensed matter-materials science laboratory. Under supervision, the students develop their own experimental ideas after investigating current research literature. With the use of sophisticated state-of-the-art instrumentation students conduct research, write a research paper, and make verbal presentations.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 211A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: General Relativity
courses.description: This is a two-quarter course on gravitation and the general theory of relativity. The first quarter is intended to be offered every year and may be taken independently of the second quarter. The second quarter will be offered in alternate years. Topics covered in the first quarter include special relativity, differential geometry, the equivalence principle, the Einstein field equations, and experimental and observational tests of gravitation theories. The second quarter will focus on more advanced topics, including gravitational collapse, Schwarzschild and Kerr geometries, black holes, gravitational radiation, cosmology, and quantum gravitation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Computational Physics II: PDE and Matrix Models
courses.description: Project-based computational physics laboratory course for modern physics and engineering problems with student’s choice of Fortran90/95 or C/C++. Applications of finite element PDE models are chosen from quantum mechanics and nanodevices, fluid dynamics, electromagnetism, materials physics, and other modern topics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussion of current research in physics of the solid state and of other condensed matter. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: High-Energy Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of current research in nuclear physics, principally in the field of elementary particles. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Plasma Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in plasma physics. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Astrophysics and Cosmology Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in astrophysics and cosmology. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Colloquium
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in physics directed to the entire physics community. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biological Physics
courses.description: The course teaches how a few fundamental models from statistical physics provide quantitative explanatory frameworks for many seemingly unrelated problems in biology. Case studies rotate from year to year and may include ion channel gating, cooperative binding, protein-DNA interaction, gene regulation, molecular motor dynamics, cytoskeletal assembly, biological electricity, population and evolutionary dynamics. May be coscheduled with PHYS 175. Students in PHYS 275 are expected to complete a report at the level of a research paper. Recommended preparation: an introduction to statistical mechanics, at least at the level of PHYS 140A or CHEM 132.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Directed Study in Physics
courses.description: Research studies under the direction of a faculty member. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Thesis Research in Physics
courses.description: Directed research on dissertation topic. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Instruction in Physics Teaching
courses.description: This course, designed for graduate students, includes discussion of teaching, techniques and materials necessary to teach physics courses. One meeting per week with course instructors, one meeting per week in an assigned recitation section, problem session, or laboratory section. Students are required to take a total of two units of PHYS 500.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in American Politics
courses.description: An undergraduate course designed to cover various aspects of American politics. May be repeated for credit two times, provided each course is a separate topic, for a maximum of twelve units.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to Legal Reasoning
courses.description: The ability to write and argue is one of the noted benefits of a legal education. Students will learn the basics of legal research and reasoning by learning to read and brief case law and write persuasive and objective memorandums.
courses.prerequisites_text: POLI 104A or 104B, upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Law and Sex
courses.description: How law regulates and impacts sexuality and orientation with focus on constitutional law in areas of privacy, free speech, association, regulation of sexual conduct under criminal law pornography, procreation, reproductive rights, and regulation of family status.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to Business Law
courses.description: This course aims to introduce students to popular topics in business law. Structured as a survey course, this course will introduce students to the nature of business entities, contract formation, drafting, negotiations, negligence, and torts, as well as topics in intellectual property and employment law. The course will be structured as a lecture course, but will also provide students with ample opportunity for hands-on interactive practice.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Global Justice in Theory and Action
courses.description: Discuss the idea of justice from multiple perspectives: theory, philosophy, institutions, markets, social mobilization, politics, and environment. Examine the assets and capabilities of diverse justice-seeking organizations and movements aimed at improving quality of life and place locally, regionally, and globally.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Game Theory in Political Science I
courses.description: This course introduces students to game theory and its uses in political science. Topics covered include the concepts of Nash equilibrium, dominant strategies, subgame perfection and backwards induction, and the applications of those concepts to the study of voting, electoral competition, public goods provision, legislatures, and collective action. An emphasis is placed on developing students’ analytical reasoning and problem-solving skills through weekly problem sets and in-class exercises.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Bending the Curve (Online): Solutions to Climate Change
courses.description: (Cross-listed with SIO 109R.) This online course focuses on developing urgent climate change solutions that integrate technology, policy and governance, finance, land use, and social/educational dimensions. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: POLI 117, POLI 117R, SIO 109, or SIO 109R.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Digital Politics
courses.description: This class will delve into the nexus of digital technology and politics. Specific topics include the impact of social media on elections and public opinion, and the use of digital tools in political spaces ranging from activism to public service provision to repression.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Consequences of Electoral Systems
courses.description: A comparative survey of the major dimensions of the electoral systems used in contemporary democracies (including plurality and majority systems, proportional representation, and districting methods) and of their effects on party competition.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics in the People’s Republic of China
courses.description: This course analyzes the political system of China since 1949, including political institutions, the policy-making process, and the relationship between politics and economics. The main focus is on the post-Mao era of reform beginning in 1978.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Weapons of Mass Destruction
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the challenges posed by chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear weapons. Students will learn about how these weapons work, why states seek them, and attempts to prevent proliferation. We will delve into technical and policy challenges related to these weapons, and address how CBRN weapons shape national and regional security dynamics. Efforts to restrict the proliferation of these weapons will be discussed. We will also analyze CBRN terrorism.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics and Warfare
courses.description: This course offers an exploration of general theories of the origins of warfare; the impact of the state on war in the modern world; and the microfoundations of combat and compliance in the context of the costs of war and military mobilization. The course should be of special interest to students in international relations and comparative politics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Insurgency and Terrorism
courses.description: “Terrorism” uses “illegitimate” violence to achieve political goals. This course uses philosophical, historical, and contemporary material from distinct cultures to understand which actions are defined as “terrorist,” who uses them, why, and when, as well as the determinants of their effectiveness.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Relations After the Cold War: Theory and Prospect
courses.description: The nature of international politics appears to have changed dramatically since 1989. This course applies different theoretical approaches to enhance our understanding of the new international environment, future prospects for peace and war, and current problems of foreign policy.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Organizations
courses.description: Surveys the theory and function of IOs (UN, NATO, EU, World Bank, IMF) in promoting international cooperation in security, peacekeeping, trade, environment, and human rights. We discuss why IOs exist, how they work, and what challenges they face.
courses.prerequisites_text: POLI 12, upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in International Relations
courses.description: An undergraduate course designed to cover various aspects of international relations. May be repeated for credit two times, provided each course is a separate topic, for a maximum of twelve units.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Advanced Social Data Analytics
courses.description: An accelerated course in computer programming and data analytics for collecting, analyzing, and understanding data in the social world. Students engage in hands-on learning with applied social science problems, developing statistical and computational skills for sophisticated data manipulation, analysis, visualization.
courses.prerequisites_text: POLI 5 or 5D or ECON 5 and POLI 30 or 30D.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Senior Honors Seminar: Frontiers of Political Science
courses.description: This course is open only to seniors interested in qualifying for departmental honors. Admission to the course will be determined by the department. Each student will write an honors essay under the supervision of a member of the faculty.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Research Seminar in Washington, DC
courses.description: (Same as COMM 194, USP 194, HITO 193, SOCI 194, COGS 194) Course attached to six-unit internship taken by students participating in the UCDC Program. Involves weekly seminar meetings with faculty and teaching assistant and a substantial research paper.
courses.prerequisites_text: participating in UCDC Program.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: Teaching and tutorial activities associated with courses and seminars. Limited to advanced political science majors with at least a 3.5 GPA in upper-division political science courses. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit two times, but only four units may be used for major credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Local Internship in Political Science
courses.description: Individual placements for field learning integrated with political science. A written contract involving all parties with learning objectives, a project outline, and a means of supervision and progress evaluation must be filed with the faculty adviser and department undergraduate coordinator prior to the beginning of the internship. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: ninety units completed; 2.5 minimum cumulative GPA overall and 3.0 in political science; POLI 30 and at least two upper-division courses in political science. Department approval and consent of instructor. Corequisites: POLI 194SD.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study in an area not presently covered by the departmental curriculum. P/NP grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading in advanced political science by individual students. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Research Design
courses.description: This course will study various approaches to knowledge accumulation in social science. A basic outline of scientific method will be used to examine the difference between theories as assumptions and axioms and hypotheses as “if-then” statements derived from theory. Experimental, quasi-experimental, and qualitative designs will be discussed.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate student standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Quantitative Methods I
courses.description: The use of quantitative methods (particularly multiple regression and its extensions) in political science. Emphasis on understanding the methods and using them in political science applications.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate student standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Relations Theory
courses.description: A survey of the principal theories and approaches to the study of international relations.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race, Class, and Institutions in American Political Economy
courses.description: This course will explore how institutions address and/or perpetuate racial, ethnic, and economic inequality in the US.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Voting and Elections
courses.description: This course is designed to acquaint graduate students with the central themes and issues in the study of voting in national elections.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Mathematical and Statistical Foundations
courses.description: This course reviews essential calculus and linear algebra and introduces probability theory (probability rules, random variables, univariate and multivariate distributions) and mathematical statistics (sampling distributions, estimation and inference frameworks).
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in Methodology
courses.description: This course offers selected topics in quantitative methodology. Content may vary each time the course is offered. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: International Law and Regulation
courses.description: Examination of recent research in international law and regulation: development and presentation of research projects by graduate students; presentation of research by faculty. Third-year students present dissertation prospectus, candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit three times as topics vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: American Politics
courses.description: Examination of recent research in American politics: development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentations of research by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: Comparative Politics
courses.description: Examination of recent research in comparative politics, development and presentation of research projects by graduate students; presentations of research projects by faculty. Third-year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: International Relations
courses.description: Examination of recent research in international relations, development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentations of research projects by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentation of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: Political Theory
courses.description: Examination of recent research in political theory: development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentation of research by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: Methodology
courses.description: Examination of recent research in political methodology; development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentation of research by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Directed Reading
courses.description: Guided and supervised reading in the literature of the several fields of political science.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.description: Independent work by graduate students engaged in research and writing of second-year paper and doctoral dissertation, under direct supervision of adviser.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the basic concepts in psychology. Topics may include human information processing, learning and memory, motivation, development, language acquisition, social psychology, and personality.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology: Biological Foundations
courses.description: This course provides an introductory survey of the relationship between human behavior and brain function. Specific areas of emphasis include vision and other sensory processes, memory, motivation, attention, and cognition.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology: Cognitive Foundations
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the basic concepts of cognitive psychology. Topics include perception, attention, memory, language, and thought. The relation of cognitive psychology to cognitive science and to neuropsychology is also covered.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology: Social Foundations
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to social psychology. Topics may include emotion, aesthetics, behavioral medicine, person perception, attitudes and attitude change, and behavior in social organizations.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Introduction to Statistics
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to both descriptive and inferential statistics, core tools in the process of scientific discovery and the interpretation of research.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of how to choose appropriate research methods for experimental and nonexperimental studies. Topics may include classic experimental design and counterbalancing, statistical power, and causal inference in experimental and nonexperimental settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 60 or equivalent.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Laboratory in Psychological Research Methods
courses.description: This course provides hands-on research experience. Lecture topics will include experimental and nonexperimental designs, research ethics, data analysis, and causal inference. Students will design original research projects, collect and analyze data, and write a full APA-style report, including a brief literature review relevant to their design. This course builds on PSYC 70 by applying design principles to students’ own research questions and ideas. Open to the following Department of Psychology majors only: PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, COGS 14B or PSYC 60 or MATH 11 and PSYC 70 or COGS 14A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Learning Sustainable Well-Being: Compassion for Self and Others
courses.description: This experiential course teaches the art of practicing psychological well-being based on principles from Eastern and Western philosophies (e.g., mindfulness, positive psychology, cognitive therapy, and neuroscience). Each week, there is a short lecture on a given topic, combined with workshop-style exercises.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or research under direction of a member of the faculty. May be taken up to three times for a maximum of twelve units.
courses.prerequisites_text: lower-division standing, completion of at least thirty units of undergraduate study at UC San Diego with a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0; completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Clinical Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the causes, characteristics, and treatment of psychological disorders. Particular emphasis is given to the interaction between biological, psychological, and sociocultural processes contributing to abnormal behavior. Students may not receive credit for both PSYC 163 and PSYC 100.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the field of developmental psychology, including topics in cognitive, language, and social development.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Sensory Neuroscience
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the neural mechanisms that support vision, audition, touch, olfaction, and taste.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the field of social psychology, covering a review of the field’s founding principles, classic findings, and a survey of recent findings. Topics will include social perception, attributions and attitudes, stereotypies, social influence, group dynamics, and aggressive and prosocial tendencies.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of cognitive psychology, the scientific study of mental processes: how people acquire, store, transform, use, and communicate information. Topics may include perception, attention, language, memory, reasoning, problem solving, decision-making, and creativity.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of human and animal behavior from a neuroscience perspective. Topics include the functions and mechanisms of perception, motivation (sex, sleep, hunger, emotions), learning and memory, and motor control and movement.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of neuroanatomy and major methods and results from neuroimaging and neuropsychological studies of behavior. Topics include attention, motor control, executive function, memory, learning, emotion, and language.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Health Sciences Research
courses.description: In this course, students explore major models in mental health research and apply them in laboratory settings, examining how team science generates knowledge and influences society. Through literature review and focused discussions on study design, methodology, and research ethics, they develop skills in critical analysis and proposal writing. If interested, students with satisfactory performance may continue research with the PI for academic credit by pursuing PSYC 199 in health sciences.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Laboratory in Clinical Psychology Research I
courses.description: This course, the first in a sequence of three courses, provides an applied examination of theory, research design, and methods for clinical research to support an independent study in research at a clinical research lab.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, PSYC 70, PSYC 100, and instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Mechanisms of Animal Behavior
courses.description: This course focuses on approaches to the study of behavior and its underlying fundamental units of analysis in human and nonhuman animals. Students may not receive credit for both PSYC 122 and PSYC 103.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Clinical Assessment and Treatment
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the history, purpose, and recent changes to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders along with appropriate evidence-based interventions. Other topics include psychiatric emergencies, crisis management, and ethics. Recommended preparation: Completion of PSYC 100.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Hormones and Behavior
courses.description: This course examines how hormones influence a variety of behaviors and how behavior reciprocally influences hormones. Specific topics covered include aggression, sex and sexuality, feeding, learning, memory, mood and neural mechanisms both in humans and nonhuman animals. Recommended preparation: completion of PSYC 106.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Cognition
courses.description: This course provides an overview of social cognition, which blends cognitive and social psychology to understand how people make sense of the social world. Topics may include social perception, inference, memory, motivation, affect, understanding the self, stereotypes, and cultural cognition.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Behavior Modification
courses.description: The course provides an extension of learning principles to human behavior. Topics include broad implications of a behavioral perspective, applied behavior analysis, and applications of behavioral principles to clinical disorders and to normal behavior in varied settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Brain Damage and Mental Function
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the neural mechanisms underlying perception, memory, language, and other mental capacities. Topics include how brain damage affects these capacities and how patients with brain lesions can contribute to our understanding of the normal brain.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Neurobiology of Learning and Memory
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the neurobiology of learning and memory, from cognitive to molecular neuroscience, including human, animal, cellular, and molecular studies of memory. Topics include amnesia, intellectual disability, exceptional intelligence, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and BILD 12 or COGS 107B or COGS 17 or PSYC 106 or PSYC 181 or PSYC 181GS or PSYC 2.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
courses.description: This course provides an overview of human sexuality research including diversity of sexual behavior and identities, sex and gender development, intimate relationships, and sexual dysfunction. Recommended preparation: completion of PSYC 1, 2, or 106.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Visual Cognition
courses.description: This course provides an overview of high-level visual perception, and of how visual perception intersects with attention, memory, and concepts. Topics may include an introduction to the visual system with an emphasis on high-level visual regions; object recognition, face recognition, scene recognition and reading; visual attention, including eye movements during scene perception and during reading; and visual working memory.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Industrial Organizational Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an examination of human behavior in industrial, business, and organizational settings. Topics include psychological principles applied to selection, placement, management, and training; the effectiveness of individuals and groups within organizations, including leadership and control; conflict and cooperation; motivation; and organizational structure and design.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychopharmacology—Drugs and Behavior
courses.description: This course provides an overview of basic principles of psychopharmacology, including psychological effects, brain mode of action, and patterns of use of psychoactive agents. Drugs discussed may include drugs of abuse and psychotherapeutics such as stimulants, opioids, sedative hypnotics, hallucinogens, marijuana, alcohol, cognitive enhancers, anxiolytics, antidepressants, and antipsychotics.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Choice and Self-Control
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the experimental analysis of choice behavior, with an emphasis on the types of choice involved in self-control. A central interest will be the conditions under which decision-making is optimal.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Impulse Control Disorders
courses.description: This course provides an overview of problems of impulse control, which are important features of major psychiatric disorders and also of atypical patterns of behavior including pathological gambling, compulsive sex, eating, exercise, and shopping. Topics include development, major common features, treatment, and neurobiological basis of impulse control disorders.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Brain, Behavior, and Evolution
courses.description: This course provides a survey of natural behaviors, including birdsong, prey capture, localization, electroreception and echolocation, and the neural system that controls them, emphasizing broad fundamental relationships between brain and behavior across species. Cross-listed with BIPN 189. Students may not receive credit for PSYC 189 and BIPN 189.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, BILD 2 or COGS 101A or COGS 107B or PSYC 102 or PSYC 106.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Topics in Psychology
courses.description: Selected topics in the field of psychology. May be taken for credit three times as topics vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology Laboratory Topics
courses.description: Selected laboratory topics in the field of psychology. May be taken for credit two times as topics vary. Open to the following majors only: PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, CG32.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, department approval, and PSYC 60 or COGS 14B or MATH 11 and PSYC 70 or COGS 14A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Honors Thesis I
courses.description: This course provides the opportunity for students to plan and carry out a research project under the guidance of the psychology faculty. Students will write a proposal for the research that they plan to conduct in 194B-C and will present this proposal to the class. Must be taken for a letter grade for the Psychology Honors Program.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 110, PSYC 111A-B, department approval, psychology majors only, acceptance to the Honors Program.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or laboratory research under direction of faculty in the Department of Psychology. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Psychology II
courses.description: The second part of a series of intensive courses in statistical methods and the mathematical treatment of data, with special reference to research in psychology.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 201A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Department Proseminar
courses.description: This course is required of all first-year students in the PhD program and serves as an introduction to the department faculty and their research programs. In this course, one psychology faculty member will lead one session on their research and area of expertise, including assigned readings of relevant journal articles.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Area Proseminar in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: A survey of basic principles and concepts of cognitive psychology. This course is intended to serve as the basic introduction for first-year students. Basic areas include knowledge, memory, thought, perception, and performance.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Sensation and Perception
courses.description: Fundamentals of vision, audition, and other senses. Emphasis will be upon psychophysical approaches to the study of these sensory modalities, as well as some essential aspects of their neurophysiological bases.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Cognitive Neural Systems (CNS)
courses.description: A weekly seminar series focused on understanding recent advances in the relationship between neural systems and behavior using a variety of experimental approaches (single unit recording, comp neuro, evolutionary bio, psychophysics, comparative anatomy, lesion work, psychopharm, fMRI, EEG, TMS, etc.). May be taken for credit twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Advanced seminar concentrating on methods of research and current experimental literature in developmental psychology. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Learning by Thinking in Children (and Adults)
courses.description: We often learn through observations or from testimony from others. Occasionally, we learn simply by thinking. How do we generate insights in the absence of new information from the external world? This course examines the cognitive capacities involved in learning by thinking, including thought experiments, deduction, analogy, imagination, and learning by explaining. This discussion-based seminar will take a cognitive science approach, emphasizing cognitive development.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Introduction to Laboratory Experimentation I
courses.description: A basic laboratory course designed to introduce first-year graduate students to experimental methods in psychology.
