The student will select a research topic; do a thorough literature review of the area; design and carry out new, original studies of problems in the selected area; and prepare a final formal report of the study at the end of the spring quarter. This course is required of all first-year graduate students in the department. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Social Psychology
courses.description: A biweekly seminar series focusing on recent advances in both basic and applied research in social psychology including topics such as interpersonal relationships, emotion, health, social cognition, judgment, and decision making. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: A weekly seminar series focused on understanding recent advances in any area of cognitive psychology. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Seminar in Communication and Information Processing
courses.description: S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: Research in psychology under supervision of individual faculty members. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit fifteen times.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: Independent research and thesis research. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit fifteen times.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: Teaching practicum for students enrolled in graduate program in psychology. Students who hold appointments as teaching assistants must enroll in this course. Minimum program requirement is for one four-unit course per year for four years. S/U grades only.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: First-year Student Seminar in Religion
courses.description: The First-year Student Seminar Program is designed to provide new students with the opportunity to explore an intellectual topic related to the study of religion with a faculty member in a small seminar setting. First-year student seminars are offered in all campus departments and undergraduate colleges, and topics vary from quarter to quarter. Enrollment is limited to fifteen to twenty students, with preference given to entering first-year students.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Devils and Demons in Christianity
courses.description: Christianity frequently finds definition in contradistinction to an “Other” characterized as immoral, irrational, and malevolent. This class investigates how devils and demons as constructions of the “Other” have contributed to Christianity’s growth and identity formation throughout history.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Special Topics in Religion
courses.description: Students in this lecture will investigate important problems in the study of religion or the history of particular religions. RELI 188 and RELI 188GS may be taken for credit for a combined total of three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: RELI
courses.title: Seminar in Religion
courses.description: This seminar requires the intensive analysis of critical problems in the study of religion or the history of particular religions. May be repeated for credit up to three times when topics vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: REV
courses.title: Revelle First-year Student Honors Program Seminar
courses.description: Weekly seminars with a faculty member (chosen each year by the provost to match the interests of participating students). This seminar will acquaint students coming from high schools (first-year students) with the scholarship and research being conducted by faculty and instill in students a sense of participation in the scholarly life at UC San Diego. P/NP grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: by invitation only. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: REV
courses.title: First-Year Student Seminar
courses.description: The First-year Seminar Program is designed to provide new students with the opportunity to explore an intellectual topic with a faculty member in a small seminar setting. First-year seminars can be offered in all campus departments and undergraduate colleges, and topics vary from quarter to quarter. Enrollment is limited to fifteen to twenty students, with preference given to entering first-year students.

courses.subject: REV
courses.title: Succeeding in Scientific Research
courses.description: This course will evaluate strategies used to select impactful topics and research questions, how to turn curiosity into knowledge by posing effective hypotheses. Practical topics—how to design an experiment, how to make effective arguments in written/spoken forms of scientific communication. P/NP grades only. (S)

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Introduction to Structures and Design
courses.description: Introduction to fundamentals of structures and how structures work. Overview of structural behavior and structural design process through hands-on projects. Lessons learned from structural failures. Professional ethics. Role and responsibility of structural engineers. Introduction to four structural engineering focus sequences. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. Enrollment restricted to SE27, SE28, SE29, SE30, and SE31 majors only.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or research under direction of a faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: student must be of first year standing and a Regents Scholar. Consent of instructor or department stamp.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Mechanics I: Statics
courses.description: Statics of particles and rigid bodies in two and three dimensions using vector representation; free body diagrams; analysis of trusses, frames, and machines; internal forces; shear force and bending moment diagrams; equilibrium problems with friction; introduction to moment of inertia.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20C or MATH 31BH and PHYS 2A or PHYS 2AR.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Mechanics III: Vibrations
courses.description: Free and forced vibrations of damped 1-DOF systems; vibrations isolation, impact and packaging problems. Analysis of discrete MDOF systems using matrix representation; normal mode of frequencies and modal matrix formulation. Lagrange’s equations. Modal superposition for analysis of continuous vibrating systems.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 31AH and SE 101B.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Structural Materials
courses.description: This course will provide lectures and labs on the structural properties of engineering materials. Topics covered will include stress and strain, strain measurement, stiffness, strength, toughness, fatigue resistance, and creep. The course will also cover different materials such as cement and concrete, woods, aluminum alloys, steel, engineering plastics, and composite materials. Corequisite: SE 110A.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 1 and SE 101A.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Statistics, Probability and Reliability
courses.description: Probability theory. Statistics, data analysis and inferential statistics, distributions, confidence intervals. Introduction to structural reliability and random phenomena. Applications to components and systems. Students will not receive credit for both SE 125 and MAE 108.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 31AH and MATH 20D. Enrollment restricted to SE27, SE28, SE29, SE30, and SE31 majors only.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Structural Analysis I
courses.description: Classical methods of analysis for statically indeterminate structures. Development of computer codes for the analysis of civil, mechanical, and aerospace structures from the matrix formulation of the classical structural theory, through the direct stiffness formulation, to production-type structural analysis programs.
courses.prerequisites_text: grade of C– or better in SE 110A.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Finite Element Analysis: Beam and Shell Models
courses.description: Project-based exploration of structural engineering computations. Topics include analysis of shell structures, design optimization, computational vibration analysis.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 131A, SE 101C, and SE 130B.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Mechanics and Design of Composite Structures
courses.description: Introduction to advanced composite materials and their applications. Fiber and matrix properties, micromechanics, stiffness, ply-by-ply stress, hygrothermal behavior, and failure prediction. Lab activity will involve design, analysis, fabrication, and testing of composite structure. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 110A or MAE 131A or MAE 131AR and SE 110B or MAE 131.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Nondestructive Evaluation
courses.description: Fourier signal processing, liquid penetrant, elastic wave propagation, ultrasonic testing, impact-echo, acoustic emission testing, vibrational testing, infrared thermography. May be coscheduled with SE 263.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 110A.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Sensors and Data Acquisition for Structural Engineering
courses.description: This course discusses theory, design, and applications of sensor technologies in the context of structural engineering and structural health monitoring. Topics include sensors and sensing mechanisms; measurement uncertainty; signal conditioning and interface circuits; data acquisition; analog/digital circuits; and emerging sensors. Students will not receive credit for both SE 164 and SE 164GS. May be coscheduled with SE 264.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 110A.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Earthquake Engineering
courses.description: Dynamic analysis of structures due to seismic ground motions. Seismic hazard, earthquake magnitude, and intensity scales. Elements of seismology. Elastic and inelastic response spectra. Modal analysis, linear and nonlinear time-history analysis. Earthquake resistant design. Seismic codes. Elements of geotechnical earthquake engineering.
courses.prerequisites_text: grade of C– or better in all SE 9, SE 101C, and SE 110A. Enrollment restricted to SE27, SE28, SE29, SE30, SE31 majors only.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Geotechnical Engineering
courses.description: General introduction to physical and engineering properties of soils. Soil classification and identification methods. Compaction and construction control. Total and effective stress. Permeability, seepage, and consolidation phenomena. Shear strength of sand and clay.
courses.prerequisites_text: grade of C– or better in SE 110A. Enrollment restricted to SE27, SE28, SE29, SE30, SE31 majors only.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Engineering Internship
courses.description: An enrichment program, available to a limited number of undergraduate students, which provides work experience with industry, government offices, etc., under the supervision of a faculty member and industrial supervisor. Coordination of the Engineering Internship is conducted through UC San Diego’s Academic Internship Program.
courses.prerequisites_text: completion of ninety units with a 2.5 GPA and consent of department chair. Department stamp required.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem by special arrangement with a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor or department stamp.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Advanced Structural Analysis
courses.description: Application of advanced analytical concepts to structural engineering problems. Analysis of frame structures using matrix methods and introduction to the finite element method. Displacement-based and force-based beam element formulations. Development of computer programs for structural analysis. Use of computer resources.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Structural Dynamics I
courses.description: Response of discrete linear structural systems to harmonic, periodic and transient excitations. Lagrangian mechanics. Linearization of the equations of motion. Free and forced vibrations of multi degree-of-freedom structures. Normal mode, frequency response and numerical methods. Continuous systems.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Advanced Structural Steel Design
courses.description: Load and Resistance Factor Design (LRFD) philosophy. Behavior and design of steel elements for global and local buckling. Background of seismic codes. Ductility requirements and capability design concept. Seismic design of steel moment frames and braced frames. Recommended preparation: SE 130A and SE 150A, or equivalent course, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Bridge Design
courses.description: Design and analysis of bridge structures, construction methods, load conditions. Load paths and distribution of dead and live loads. Service, strength, and extreme event limit states and other load and resistance factor design (LRFD) principles. Design of prestressed concrete bridges. Special problems in analysis—concrete box girders, curved and skewed bridges, environmental and seismic loads. Conceptual/preliminary bridge design project. Recommended preparation: SE 151A-B, SE 201A, SE 211, SE 223, or equivalent courses.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Seismic Isolation and Energy Dissipation
courses.description: Concepts, advantages, and limitations of seismic isolation techniques; fundamentals of dynamic response under seismic excitation; spectral analysis; damping; energy approach; application to buildings and structures.
courses.prerequisites_text: SE 221 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Computational Techniques in Finite Elements
courses.description: Cross-listed with MAE 235. Practical application of the finite element method to problems in solid mechanics. Elements of theory are presented as needed. Covered are static and dynamic heat transfer and stress analysis. Basic processing, solution methods, and postprocessing are practiced with commercial finite element software. Students may not receive credit for SE 233 and MAE 235.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
courses.description: Advanced treatment of topics in soil mechanics, including state of stress, pore pressure, consolidation and settlement analysis, shear strength of cohesionless and cohesive soils, mechanisms of ground improvement, and slope stability analysis. Concepts in course reinforced by laboratory experiments.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Numerical Methods in Geomechanics
courses.description: Application of finite element method to static and dynamic analysis of geotechnical structures. One-, 2-, and 3-D static and seismic response of earth structures/slopes/Foundation systems. Pore-pressure generation/effects during cycle loading. System identification using strong motion downhole-array data. Use of computer resources required.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Mechanics and Design of Composite Structures
courses.description: Graduate-level introduction to advanced composite materials and their applications. Fiber and matrix properties, 3D properties, stress-strain relationships, micromechanics, stiffness, ply-by-ply stress, classical laminated plate theory, hygrothermal/CTE behavior, and failure prediction. Lab activity will involve composite fabrication methods and design, analysis, build, and testing of composite structure. May be coscheduled with SE 142. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Nondestructive Evaluation
courses.description: Fourier signal processing, liquid penetrant, elastic wave propagation, ultrasonic testing, impact-echo, acoustic emission testing, vibrational testing, infrared thermography. May be coscheduled with SE 163. Recommended Preparation: undergraduate degree in structural, civil, mechanical, or aerospace engineering.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Sensors and Data Acquisition for Structural Engineering
courses.description: This course discusses theory, design, and applications of sensor technologies in the context of structural engineering and structural health monitoring. Topics include sensors and sensing mechanisms; measurement uncertainty; signal conditioning and interface circuits; data acquisition; analog/digital circuits; and emerging sensors. May be coscheduled with SE 164.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Finite Element Methods in Solid Mechanics I
courses.description: Finite element methods for linear problems in solid mechanics. Emphasis on the principle of virtual work, finite element stiffness matrices, various finite element formulations and their accuracy and the numerical implementation required to solve problems in small strain, isotropic elasticity in solid mechanics.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Structural Optimization
courses.description: Construction of structural design as an optimization problem; mathematical programming for sizing, shape, and topology; linear and nonlinear programming; continuous and discrete optimization methods; Lagrangian function and KKT optimality condition; MATLAB. Use of computer resources.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Structural Engineering Seminar
courses.description: Weekly seminar and discussion by faculty, visitors, postdoctoral research fellows and graduate students concerning research topics in earthquake engineering and related subjects. May be repeated for credit. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Graduate Research
courses.description: (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: SE
courses.title: Teaching Experience
courses.description: Teaching experience in an appropriate SE undergraduate course under direction of the faculty member in charge of the course. Lecturing one hour per week in either a problem-solving section or regular lecture.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and the department. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: The Planets
courses.description: Space exploration has revealed an astonishing diversity among the planets and moons in our solar system. The planets and their histories will be compared to gain insight and a new perspective on planet Earth.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Life in the Oceans
courses.description: An introduction to the wide variety of organisms that live in the oceans, the habitats they occupy, and how species interact with each other and their environment. Included will be examinations of adaptations, behavior, ecology, and a discussion of local and global resource management and conservation issues. This course is designed for nonbiology majors.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Natural Disasters
courses.description: Introduction to environmental perils and their impact on everyday life. Geological and meteorological processes, including earthquakes, volcanic activity, large storms, global climate change, mass extinctions throughout Earth’s history, and human activity that causes and prevents natural disasters.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: The Atmosphere
courses.description: This course describes the distinguishing features of the Earth’s atmosphere, providing a nontechnical overview of the role of the atmosphere in meteorology and climate sciences. Topics include atmospheric structure, global temperature trends and their causes, water-temperature relationships, the ozone layer and hole, Earth’s radiation balance forecasting transport and storms, greenhouse gas effects, aerosols and clouds, precipitation and acid rain, and climate change. Students may not receive credit for both SIO 20 and SIO 20R.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: The Oceans
courses.description: Presents modern ideas and descriptions of the physical, chemical, biological, and geological aspects of oceanography, and considers the interactions between these aspects. Intended for students interested in the oceans, but who do not necessarily intend to become professional scientists.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Life and Climate on Earth
courses.description: Explores life on Earth and its relationship to the environment—past, present, and future. Topics include origins of life, earth history, elemental cycles, global climate variability and human impacts on our environment.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Introduction to Physical Geology
courses.description: This course is an introduction to how our planet works, focusing on the formation and evolution of the solid earth, and the processes affecting both its surface and interior. Laboratories and substantial field component complement and extend the lecture material. Program and/or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: First-year Seminar
courses.description: The First-year Seminar Program is designed to provide the new students with the opportunity to explore an intellectual topic with a faculty member in a small setting. First-year seminars can be offered in all campus departments and undergraduate colleges, and topics vary from quarter to quarter. Enrollment is limited to fifteen to twenty students, with preference given to entering first-year students. Students may complete up to four first-year seminars with the stipulation that none of the seminars are repeated. (P/NP grades only).

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar
courses.description: Perspectives on ocean sciences. This seminar introduces students to exciting and current research topics in ocean science as presented by faculty and researchers at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. Formerly ERTH 90.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem by special arrangement with a faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: lower-division standing, completion of thirty units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0, and a completed and approved Special Studies form, UC San Diego Application for Enrollment Special Studies Courses 97, 98, 99.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: California Coastal Oceanography
courses.description: This course emphasizes oceanographic connections between physical and climate forcing and marine ecosystem responses using examples from and activities in the California coastal environment. The approach is inquiry-based, combining classroom and experiential learning to build critical and quantitative thinking and research insights and abilities.
courses.prerequisites_text: CHEM 6A or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Geochemistry
courses.description: An introduction to the chemical composition and evolution of the Earth and solar system. Applications of chemical methods to elucidate the origin and geologic history of the Earth and the planets, evolution of oceans and atmosphere, and human environmental impacts.
courses.prerequisites_text: SIO 50 and CHEM 6A-B-C or CHEM 6AH-6BH-6CH, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Introduction to Geophysics
courses.description: An introduction to the structure and composition of the solid earth. Topics include seismology, the gravity and magnetic fields, high-pressure geophysics, and concepts in geodynamics. Emphasis is on global geophysics, i.e., on the structure and evolution of the planet.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20C or MATH 31BH, and PHYS 2C, and SIO 50, or consent of instructor. SIO 160 recommended.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Sedimentology and Stratigraphy
courses.description: This course will examine sedimentary environments from mountain tops to the deep sea across a variety of time scales. The focus is to develop the skills to interpret stratigraphy and read the history of the Earth that it records. Laboratories and substantial field component complement and extend lecture material. Program and/or course materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: SIO 50 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Bending the Curve Online: Climate Change Solutions
courses.description: (Cross-listed with POLI 117R). This online course focuses on developing urgent climate change solutions that integrate technology, policy and governance, finance, land-use, and social/educational dimensions. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: POLI 117, POLI 117R, SIO 109, or SIO 109R.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: The Physical Basis of Global Warming
courses.description: Introduction to the processes behind global warming, including the physics of the greenhouse effect, controls on greenhouse gases, atmospheric and oceanic circulation, climate feedbacks, relationship to natural climate variability, and global environmental issues related to global warming.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20D and PHYS 2C or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Biomechanics of Marine Life
courses.description: An introduction to the physical basis of the biological world. This course explores how the physical principles of solids and fluids underlay the functional morphology, ecology, and adaptations of all living things, with emphasis on marine organisms.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 3 and PHYS 1C or PHYS 2C, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Introduction to Marine Biology
courses.description: Overview of marine organisms and their adaptations to sea life. Selected examples of physiological, behavioral, and evolutionary adaptations in response to the unique challenges of a maritime environment.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 3 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Marine Biology Laboratory
courses.description: Introductory laboratory course in current principles and techniques applicable to research problems in marine biology. Field component includes introduction to intertidal, salt marsh, or other marine ecosystems. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 3, SIO 132, and SIO 134, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Applications of Phylogenetics
courses.description: Because life’s history spans macroevolutionary time scales, challenging direct study, we rely on indirect tools like phylogenetics. The first part of the course covers phylogenetic inference theory, encompassing principles and applications. Part two delves into phylogenetic comparative methods, employing trees for macroevolutionary inference. These methods explore global biodiversity, diversification rates, and morphological evolution. The course also features a substantial computer lab component.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 3 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Archaeology—Theory and Method of Socioecodynamics and Human Paleoecology
courses.description: Introduction to the multidisciplinary tools for paleoenvironmental analysis—from ecology, sedimentology, climatology, zoology, botany, chemistry, and others—and provides the theory and method to investigate the dynamics between human behavior and natural processes. This socioecodynamic perspective facilitates a nuanced understanding of topics such as resource overexploitation, impacts on biodiversity, social vulnerability, sustainability, and responses to climate change. Students may not receive credit for ANAR 166 and SIO 166.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Volcanology
courses.description: This class will introduce students to the fundamentals of the science of volcanology. Topics explored will include the processes and products of various types of volcanism, magma genesis, eruptive mechanisms, in addition to volcanic monitoring, hazards and mitigation. Students may not receive credit for both SIO 170 and SIO 170GS.
courses.prerequisites_text: SIO 100 and CHEM 6A or CHEM 6AH, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Introduction to Physical Oceanography
courses.description: A physical description of the sea at the upper-division level, with emphasis on currents, waves, and turbulent motions that are observed in the ocean, and on the physics governing them.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20C and PHYS 2C or PHYS 4C, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Analysis of Oceanic and Atmospheric Data
courses.description: Oceanic and atmospheric observations produce large data sets whose understanding requires analysis using computers. This course will include an introduction to MATLAB for the purpose of analyzing data. Students will use modern data sets from the ocean and atmosphere to learn statistical data analysis.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 18 or MATH 20F or MATH 31AH or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Fluid Dynamics
courses.description: This course gives an introduction to ocean and atmosphere fluid properties, statics, and kinematics; fluid conservation laws; irrotational flow; Bernoulli equation; gravity waves; shallow water equations; geophysical applications.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A and MATH 20D and MATH 20E or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Ocean Instruments and Sensors
courses.description: Apply modern and classic techniques for analysis of seawater, introducing concepts of signal transduction, calibration, and measurement quality control. Emphasis will be placed on computer automation to perform basic functions including instrument control, data storage, and on-the-fly calculations. Students will apply techniques from several branches of engineering to the marine sciences. Students may not receive credit for both SIO 179 and SIO 190 with the same subtitle. Recommended preparation: PHYS 2A-C or PHYS 4A-C. Prerequisites : CHEM 6A or CHEM 6AH or PHYS 2A or PHYS 4A or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Biology of Fishes
courses.description: The comparative evolution, morphology, physiology, and ecology of fishes. Special emphasis on local, deep-sea, and pelagic forms in laboratory.
courses.prerequisites_text: BILD 3 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Pollution, Environment and Health
courses.description: The goal is to understand the scope of the pollution problem facing the planet. Students will learn the properties of chemicals in the environment and survey the biological mechanisms that determine their accumulation and toxicity.
courses.prerequisites_text: CHEM 6C and BILD 1 or 3 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Special Topics in Earth, Oceans, and Atmosphere—Lab
courses.description: A lab course designed to treat emerging or topical subjects in the earth, ocean, or atmospheric sciences. Involves lectures, lab work, reading from the literature, and student participation in discussion.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Research Seminar in Washington, DC
courses.description: Course attached to a six- to eight-unit internship taken by students participating in the UCDC Program. Involves weekly seminar meetings with faculty and teaching assistant and a substantial research paper.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval. Participation in the UCDC Program during quarter enrolled in seminar.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Honors Thesis Research
courses.description: Course is for student participants in the senior honors thesis research program. Students complete individual research on a problem by special arrangement with, and under the direction of, a Scripps Institution of Oceanography faculty member. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: completed ninety units of courses, including twelve units of SIO courses. Achieved a GPA of 3.3 overall and 3.5 in SIO courses. Submitted to Scripps Steering Committee, and had approved, an honors thesis research proposal. Department stamp.

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem. By special arrangement with a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)

courses.subject: SIO
courses.title: Research
courses.description: (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: SIOB
courses.title: Ocean Law and Policy
courses.description: This course provides an overview of key laws and policies governing US and international ocean and coastal waters, examines timely case studies of policies in practice, brings a variety of perspectives to illustrate complexities of policy making, and combines lectures with student presentations and in-class exercises. Reading materials are assigned, including statutes, case law, media publications, and law review articles. Students will develop critical thinking, writing, and public speaking skills.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOB
courses.title: Marine Chemical Biology Seminar
courses.description: Students will give seminars on current research topics that span the interface of marine chemistry and marine biology. Topics will include natural products chemistry, biotechnology, biogeochemistry, and biochemistry relating to marine systems. May be taken for credit eighteen times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: SIOB
courses.title: Professional Ethics in Science
courses.description: A seminar on the historical and contemporary ethics and ethos of scientific research, based on published documents. Given in alternate years.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOB
courses.title: Benthic Ecology
courses.description: Evolution and maintenance of benthic communities from the terrestrial margins to the deep sea. Special emphasis will be placed on physical and biological scaling and processes determining patterns of distribution and abundance; interrelationships between community structure and population phenomena, including trophic relationships, reproductive and recruitment patterns, succession, and life history biology. Offered in alternate years with SIOB 275B.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: SIOB
courses.title: Seminar in Ocean Biosciences
courses.description: Presentations of reports, review of literature, and discussion of current research in the marine biological and oceanographic sciences. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: SIOB
courses.title: Ecology Seminar in Biological Oceanography
courses.description: Weekly seminar for students in the biological oceanography curricular group. Lectures given by visiting scientists, resident staff, and students. May be taken for credit eighteen times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. (S/U grades only)

courses.subject: SIOB
courses.title: Biological Oceanography
courses.description: The biology and ecology of marine plankton, nekton, and benthos. Emphasis will be on processes regulating species, community, and ecosystem patterns and changes, including productivity, trophic relationships and species interactions with the physical, chemical, and geological environment. One or more field trips.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOB
courses.title: Marine Physiology
courses.description: Biochemical and physiological mechanisms of adaptation of organisms to the marine environment. Special emphasis is on biological responses to temperature, salinity, carbon dioxide, pH and bicarbonate levels.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOB
courses.title: Physical-Biological Interactions
courses.description: Physical and biological processes affecting growth and patchiness of plankton. Concepts and equations from physical oceanography will be presented and explored in a biological context. Ideas will be treated both theoretically and with examples from the literature.
courses.prerequisites_text: SIOC 210 or SIO 210 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOB
courses.title: Marine Biology Seminar
courses.description: Lectures given by visiting scientists and resident staff and students. May be taken for credit eighteen times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Introduction to Applied Mathematics I
courses.description: (Cross-listed with MAE 294A.) Review of exact methods for ordinary differential equations. Expansions about regular and irregular singular points, eigenfunction methods for ordinary differential equations, special functions, Fourier series and integral transforms, linear algebra.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Underwater Acoustics
courses.description: Theory of radiation, transmission, and scattering of sound with special application to ocean acoustics.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Introduction to Digital Signal Processing
courses.description: Discussion of discrete-time signals and systems, Discrete-Time Fourier Transform (DFT) and window functions, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), design of Finite Impulse Response (FIR) and Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) digital filters and their implementations, finite word length effects, applications to data acquisition and analysis. May be coscheduled with ECE 161A.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Seminar in Applied Ocean Sciences
courses.description: Topics in applied ocean sciences. One-hour seminar. (S/U grades only).

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Within the next few years, lectures on various special subjects will be offered by members of the staff. The emphasis will be on topics that reveal the interdependence of the biological, chemical, geological, and physical processes operating in the oceans. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Physical Oceanography
courses.description: Physical description of the sea; physical properties of seawater, methods and measurements, boundary processes, regional oceanography.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Introduction to Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: A survey of classical problems in fluid mechanics and approximate techniques of analysis. Topics include conservation equations, straight laminar flows, low and high Reynolds number laminar flow, stability of laminar flows, turbulent flow.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Atmospheric and Climate Sciences I
courses.description: Thermodynamics and statics of dry and moist air, atmospheric composition, Earth radiation budget, vertical structure of the atmosphere, global energy balance, thermodynamic feedbacks in the climate system.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (Letter grades only.)

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Cloud Dynamics and Climate
courses.description: Cloud identification, cloud properties, dynamical processes governing formation and dissipation of different cloud types, impact of clouds on radiation flux and climate.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing and SIOC 217A or SIO 217A and SIOC 217B or SIO 217B. Nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Analysis of Physical Oceanographic Data (A)
courses.description: Fundamental elements of analysis of geophysical and oceanographic time series, including sampling problems, least squares techniques, spectral analysis, interpretation of series, design of experiments.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Underwater Bioacoustics
courses.description: Introductory course to familiarize a broad spectrum of participants to underwater sound and its relationship to underwater animals. Basic physics of sound propagation, use of sound to study underwater animals, and the sounds made by the animals themselves for echolocation and communication will be covered.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOC
courses.title: Proposal Writing and Oceanographic Experiment Design
courses.description: Students will use concepts developed in class to develop ideas for an observational experiment, culminating in the writing of an NSF-style proposal and oral presentation of the proposed project. This effort will include identification of a tractable scientific problem, background research, development of an appropriate measurement program, and the writing of a compelling science proposal. Course will provide an opportunity to synthesize scientific, technical, and practical concepts presented in class.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOG
courses.title: Geophysics Research Skills II—Effective Presentation Techniques
courses.description: This course reviews basic oral presentation skills (with and without slides), including overall structure of a presentation, how to prepare and how to deliver an effective talk. The course also covers effective figure design and color schemes.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: SIOG
courses.title: Geophysical Data Analysis I
courses.description: Probability and statistics and their application to make inferences from geophysical data: point processes, distributions, maximum likelihood estimation, hypothesis testing and confidence intervals, least squares, density estimation, interpolation and smoothing.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOG
courses.title: Physics of Earth Materials
courses.description: Mathematics and physics of continuous media, focusing on geophysical problems. Topics include deformation, stress, conservation laws, elasticity, attenuation, viscoelasticity, fracture mechanics, and porous media.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SIOG
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: A three-quarter required sequence for the BS/MS in marine biology, geosciences, and ocean and atmospheric sciences students to prepare for the undergraduate-to-graduate transition and thesis preparation. The course will cover fundamental issues in academia, including campus resources, research design, scientific publishing, and how to write and defend an MS thesis. The course will also support community building and networking among the current BS/MS students at SIO.
courses.prerequisites_text: current SIO department BS/MS student. Department approval required. Must be taken for letter grade only.

courses.subject: SIOG
courses.title: Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations
courses.description: The course will discuss main numerical methods used to solve boundary and initial value problems involving partial differential equations, such as finite differences, finite elements, and boundary elements. The emphasis will be on practical implementation of the commonly used tools and algorithms. Examples from geophysical applications will be provided. Recommended preparation: calculus and linear algebra.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: SIOG
courses.title: Marine Geology
courses.description: Introduction to the geomorphology, sedimentation, stratigraphy, volcanism, structural geology, tectonics, and geological history of the oceans.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: SOCG
courses.title: Political Sociology
courses.description: This course discusses the relationship between state and society in a comparative perspective. The focus is on the interaction among states, domestic economic elites, and external economic and political processes in the determination of different developmental paths. Analytically, it includes topics such as characteristics and functions of the state in different types of society throughout history (with an emphasis on the varieties of capitalist and socialist state), the autonomy of the state and its causes in different settings, and developmental and predatory consequences of state activity. Readings will include both theoretical and empirical materials, the latter dealing mostly with nineteenth- and twentieth-century Europe and twentieth-century Latin America.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in sociology.

courses.subject: SOCG
courses.title: Research Practicum I
courses.description: In this seminar students work on a research project, which might have originated in a paper written for another course. The goal is to produce the first draft of a paper that will be submitted to an academic journal.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in sociology.

courses.subject: SOCG
courses.title: Research Practicum II
courses.description: In this seminar students revise an existing research paper (usually the one they wrote for Sociology 252) for submission to an academic journal. Emphasis is placed on conceptual development, writing style and structure, and drawing links to the existing theoretical and empirical literature.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in sociology.

courses.subject: SOCG
courses.title: Colloquium in Science Studies
courses.description: (Same as Phil 209C, HIGR 240, and COGR 225C.) A forum for the presentation and discussion of research in progress in science studies, by graduate students, faculty, and visitors. Required of all students in the Science Studies Program.
courses.prerequisites_text: enrollment in the Science Studies Program.

courses.subject: SOCG
courses.title: Graduate Seminar
courses.description: A research seminar in special topics of interest to available staff, provides majors and minors in sociology with research experience in close cooperation with faculty. (S/U grades permitted.)
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in sociology.

courses.subject: SOCG
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Tutorial individual guides study and/or independent research in an area not covered by present course offerings. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in sociology; department approval.

courses.subject: SOCG
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Open to graduate students engaged in thesis research. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in sociology.

courses.subject: SOCG
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: Supervised teaching in lower-division contact classes, supplemented by seminar on methods in teaching sociology. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing in sociology. Technology done under the direction of a faculty member. College stamp required. Pass/Not Pass grade only.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
courses.description: An introduction to the organizing themes and ideas, empirical concerns, and analytical approaches of the discipline of sociology. The course focuses on both classical and contemporary views of modern society, on the nature of community, and on inequality, with special attention to class, race, and gender. Materials include both theoretical statements and case studies. Will not receive credit for SOCI 1 and SOCL 1A.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Science, Technology, and Society
courses.description: A series of case studies of the relations between society and modern science, technology, and medicine. Global warming, reproductive medicine, AIDS, and other topical cases prompt students to view science-society interactions as problematic and complex. Will not receive credit for SOCI 30 and SOCL 30.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Introduction to Law and Society
courses.description: Interrelationships between law and society, in the U.S. and other parts of the world. We examine law’s norms, customs, culture, and institutions, and explain the proliferation of lawyers in the U.S. and the expansion of legal “rights” worldwide. Will not receive credit for SOCI 50 and SOCL 50.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: The Practice of Social Research
courses.description: This course introduces students to the fundamental principles of the design of social research. It examines the key varieties of evidence, sampling methods, logic of comparison, and causal reasoning researchers use in their study of social issues. Will not receive credit for SOCI 60 and SOCL 60.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Classical Sociological Theory
courses.description: Major figures and schools in sociology from the early nineteenth century onwards, including Marx, Tocqueville, Durkheim, and Weber. The objective of the course is to provide students with a background in classical social theory, and to show its relevance to contemporary sociology.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 100 and SOCA 100.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Field Research: Methods of Participant Observation
courses.description: Relationship between sociological theory and field research. Strong emphasis on theory and methods of participant observation: consideration of problems of entry into field settings, recording observations, description/analysis of field data, ethical problems in fieldwork. Required paper using field methods.
courses.prerequisites_text: SOCI 60 and upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 104 and SOCA 104.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Qualitative Interviewing
courses.description: This course provides students with tools to conduct original research using qualitative interviews. Students will learn how to prepare, conduct, and analyze qualitative interviews. Special emphasis will be placed on the presentation of research in written form.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 104Q and SOCA 104Q.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: This course will deal with human behavior and personality development as affected by social group life. Major theories will be compared. The interaction dynamics of such substantive areas as socialization, normative and deviant behavior, learning and achievement, the social construction of the self, and the social identities will be considered.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 112 and SOCB 112.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Language, Culture, and Education
courses.description: (Same as EDS 117.) The mutual influence of language, culture, and education will be explored; explanations of students’ school successes and failures that employ linguistic and cultural variables will be considered; bilingualism; cultural transmission through education.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 117 and SOCB 117.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Special Topics in Culture, Language, and Social Interaction
courses.description: This course will examine key issues in culture, language, and social interaction. Content will vary from year to year.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Social Networks
courses.description: This course takes a social network approach to the study of society, examining the complex web of relationships— platonic, familial, professional, romantic—in which individual behavior is embedded. Special emphasis is placed on the unprecedented opportunities created by contemporary social media (e.g., Facebook, mobile phones, online dating websites) for answering fundamental sociological questions.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Japanese Culture Inside/Out: A Transnational Perspective
courses.description: We examine cultural production in Japan and abroad, national and transnational political-economic and social influences, the idea of Japan in the West, and the idea of the West in Japan.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of Immigration
courses.description: Immigration from a comparative, historical, and cultural perspective. Topics include factors influencing amount of immigration and destination of immigrants; varying modes of incorporation of immigrants; immigration policies and rights; the impact of immigration on host economies; refugees; assimilation; and return migration.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 125 and SOCB 125.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Social Organization of Education
courses.description: (Same as EDS 126.) The social organization of education in the U.S. and other societies; the functions of education for individuals and society; the structure of schools; educational decision making; educational testing; socialization and education; formal and informal education; cultural transmission.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 126 and SOCC 126.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: The Making of Modern Medicine
courses.description: A study of the social, intellectual, and institutional aspects of the nineteenth-century transformation of clinical medicine, examining both the changing content of medical knowledge and therapeutics, and the organization of the medical profession.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 134 and SOCC 134A.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Medical Sociology
courses.description: An inquiry into the roles of culture and social structure in mediating the health and illness experiences of individuals and groups. Topics include the social construction of illness, the relationships between patients and health professionals, and the organization of medical work.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 135 and SOCC 135.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of Food
courses.description: Topics include food as a marker of social differences (e.g., gender, class, ethnicity); the changing character of food production and distribution; food as an object of political conflict; and the symbolic meanings and rituals of food preparation and consumption.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 137 and SOCB 137.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Genetics and Society
courses.description: The class will first examine the direct social effects of the “genetic revolution”: eugenics, genetic discrimination, and stratification. Second, the implications of thinking of society in terms of genetics, specifically—sociobiology, social Darwinism, evolutionary psychology, and biology.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 138 and SOCC 138 or SOCI 138 and SOCI 138GS.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of Law
courses.description: This course analyzes the functions of law in society, the social sources of legal change, social conditions affecting the administration of justice, and the role of social science in jurisprudence.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 140 and SOCC 140.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Law and Society in China
courses.description: This course offers an overview of the courts of China. The focus is not on blackletter law. Instead, we look at what grassroots courts do on a daily basis. China has arguably the largest court system in the world. What does it do? How are the courts organized internally? What is the relationship between the courts and other government bureaucracies? Is there the rule of law in China? The course will address these questions by reviewing latest empirical research on the subject area.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Crime and Society
courses.description: A study of the social origins of criminal law, the administration of justice, causes, and patterns of criminal behavior, and the prevention and control of crime, including individual rehabilitation and institutional change, and the politics of legal, police, and correctional reform.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 141 and SOCC 141.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Social Deviance
courses.description: This course studies the major forms of behavior seen as rule violations by large segments of our society and analyzes the major theories trying to explain them, as well as processes of rulemaking, rule enforcing, techniques of neutralization, stigmatization and status degradation, and rule change.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 142 and SOCB 142.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Love
courses.description: This course examines the complex historical, cultural, and social psychological landscape surrounding the concept of romantic (as opposed to platonic or familial) love, culminating with a critical analysis of the changing nature of intimate relationships in modern American society. Accordingly, this course will address concepts and insights at the intersection of many subfields: culture, gender, sexuality, family, social networks, social psychology, and computer-mediated communication.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Violence and Society
courses.description: Focusing on American history, this course explores violence in the light of three major themes: struggles over citizenship and nationhood; the drawing and maintenance of racial, ethnic, and gender boundaries; and the persistence of notions of “masculinity” and its relation to violence.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 145 and SOCB 145.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Political Sociology
courses.description: Course focuses on the interaction between state and society. It discusses central concepts of political sociology (social cleavages, mobilization, the state, legitimacy), institutional characteristics, causes, and consequences of contemporary political regimes (liberal democracies, authoritarianism, communism), and processes of political change.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 148 and SOCC 148.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Madness and the Movies
courses.description: Hollywood has had an ongoing obsession with mental illness. This course will examine a number of important or iconic films on this subject. By examining them against a background provided by relevant scholarly materials, we shall develop a critical perspective on these cultural artifacts.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 150 and SOCC 150.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of Religion
courses.description: Diverse sociological explanations of religious ideas and religious behavior. The social consequences of different kinds of religious beliefs and religious organizations. The influence of religion upon concepts of history, the natural world, human nature, and the social order. The significance of such notions as “sacred peoples” and “sacred places.” The religious-like character of certain political movements and certain sociocultural attitudes.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 156 and SOCC 156.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Predicting the Future from Tarot Cards to Computer Algorithms
courses.description: No one can see the future but everyone must try. When we act with purpose, we must form an idea of the consequences of our actions and the world in which our action will unfold. We must form expectations about the future, and therefore, we must predict, often in the face of great uncertainty, what will and won’t happen. This course surveys the social devices from tarot cards to computer algorithms designed to solve the problem of prediction.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Sociology of Health, Illness, and Medicine
courses.description: This course will explore the social forces that shape our health and the way we understand illness. Themes will include American public health and health care, inequality and biomedicine, as well as special topics like suicide, lead, autism, and HIV/AIDS.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Social Movements and Social Protest
courses.description: An examination of the nature of protests and violence, particularly as they occur in the context of larger social movements. The course will further examine those generic facets of social movements having to do with their genesis, characteristic forms of development, relationship to established political configurations, and gradual fading away.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 180 and SOCC 180.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: African Societies through Film
courses.description: Exploration of contemporary African urbanization and social change via film, including 1) transitional African communities, 2) social change in Africa, 3) Western vs. African filmmakers’ cultural codes. Ideological and ethnographic representations, aesthetics, social relations, and market demand for African films are analyzed.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 187 and SOCD 187.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Latin America: Society and Politics
courses.description: Course focuses on the different types of social structures and political systems in Latin America. Topics include positions in the world economy, varieties of class structure and ethnic cleavages, political regimes, mobilization and legitimacy, class alignments, reform and revolution.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 188D and SOCD 188D.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Community and Social Change in Africa
courses.description: The process of social change in African communities, with emphasis on changing ways of seeing the world and the effects of religion and political philosophies of social change. The methods and data used in various village and community studies in Africa will be critically examined.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Will not receive credit for SOCI 188E and SOCD 188A.

courses.subject: SOCI
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Tutorial: individual study under the direction of an interested faculty member in an area not covered by the present course offerings. Approval must be secured from the departmental committee on independent studies.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval required.

courses.subject: SPPS
courses.title: Acute Care Adv Pharm Pract Exp

courses.subject: SYN
courses.title: Inquiring about a Changing Planet
courses.description: Synthesis 2 builds upon the skills developed in Synthesis 1. In the first half of the quarter, students learn the links between climate change and racial justice. Using an antiracist framework, students work in a small group to research an aspect of the climate crisis. In the second half of the quarter, students are introduced to project design and learn how to draft a proposal. Students learn how to determine the scope of a project based on such criteria as time, money, and potential impact.
courses.prerequisites_text: Seventh College students only, SYN 1/1R, must be taken for a letter grade to count toward Seventh College general-education requirements. Duplicate credit with SYN 2R.

courses.subject: SYN
courses.title: Engaging with a Changing Planet
courses.description: SYN 100 is a project-based course that builds upon foundational skills by taking a collaborative, interdisciplinary approach to complex global problems. Each section focuses on a different theme, challenge, or question related to the climate crisis. Despite the different class topics, all students will learn by designing and executing a team project that addresses their section’s theme.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to Seventh College students only, upper-division standing, completion of SYN 1/1R and SYN 2/2R, must be taken for a letter grade to count toward Seventh College general-education requirements.

courses.subject: SYN
courses.title: Defining the Scope of a Changing Planet
courses.description: SYN 150 is recommended for Seventh College transfer students in preparation for SYN 100. Students critically examine, through an interdisciplinary and antiracist lens, key issues impacting our changing planet.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to Seventh College transfer students only, must be taken for a letter grade to count toward Seventh College high-impact requirement, cannot be taken concurrently or after SYN 100. Duplicate credit with SYN 150R.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Introduction to Acting
courses.description: A beginning course in the fundamentals of acting: establishing a working vocabulary and acquiring the basic skills of the acting process. Through exercises, compositions, and improvisations, the student actor explores the imagination as the actor’s primary resource, and the basic approach to text through action.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Acting I
courses.description: This course focuses on beginning scene study with an emphasis on exploring action/objective and the given circumstances of a selected text.
courses.prerequisites_text: THAC or TDAC 1 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Classical Text
courses.description: Studies in the heightened realities of poetic drama. Verse analysis, research, methods and how to approach a classical dialogue.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDAC 102.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Chekhov Acting
courses.description: Practical exercises, discussion, text analysis, and scene work on the writings of Anton Chekhov. Admission by audition/interview.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDAC 102.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Advanced Topics
courses.description: Advanced topics in acting, such as avant-garde drama, commedia, or Beckett, for students who possess basic acting techniques. May be taken for credit four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDAC 102.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Movement for Actors
courses.description: An exploration of the wide array of physical skills necessary for the actor. Using techniques derived from mime, clowning, sports, acrobatics, and improvisation, students will investigate their individual physical potential as well as their sense of creativity and imagination.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDAC 101.

courses.subject: TDAC
courses.title: Ensemble: Undergraduate Production
courses.description: Participation in a fully staged theatre production directed by an MFA or PhD student for the Department of Theatre and Dance. Admission by audition only.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of the instructor; department stamp.

courses.subject: TDDE
courses.title: Introduction to Design for the Theatre
courses.description: A survey of contemporary and historical concepts and practices in the visual arts of the theatre; studies in text analysis, studio processes and technical production; elementary work in design criticism, scale model making, and costume design. A course serving as an introduction to theatre design and production.

courses.subject: TDDE
courses.title: Theatre Process—Costume Design
courses.description: The process of the costume designer from script analysis and research visualization of ideas, through the process of costume design. Lecture and demonstration labs parallel lecture material. This course is intended for those interested in a basic understanding of the costumer’s process. No previous drawing or painting skills required.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDE 1.

courses.subject: TDDE
courses.title: Assistant Designer
courses.description: A production-oriented course that continues to introduce students to the fundamentals of design assisting. Laboratory format allows the student to work with faculty, graduate, or advanced undergraduate theatre designers, doing research, developing design concepts, and supporting the designer in a number of professional ways. May be taken for credit up to six times for a maximum of twelve units. A maximum of eight total units may be used towards major requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDE 1; consent of instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: TDDE
courses.title: Special Topics in Theatre Design
courses.description: A course designed to expose the theatre design students to a variety of specialized topics that will vary from quarter to quarter. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDE 1 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDDE
courses.title: Undergraduate Main Stage Production: Design
courses.description: A course that will guide a student in a design assignment on the undergraduate main stage production. Specialized topics dependent on the design requirements of the production. Students may repeat this course a maximum of six times or can receive up to twelve units, whichever is met first. A maximum of eight total units may be used towards major requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDE 1 and TDDE 101 or TDDE 111 or TDDE 121 or TDDE 131, or consent of instructor. Instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: TDDM
courses.title: Introduction to Dance Making
courses.description: Explores the concepts and processes of dance making through creative projects, discussions, and the examination of major dance works. Recommended preparation: No prior dance experience required. Open to all levels.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDDR
courses.title: Stage Management
courses.description: Discussion and research into the duties, responsibilities, and roles of a stage manager. Work to include studies in script analysis, communication, rehearsal procedures, performance skills, and style and conceptual approach to theatre. THGE or TDGE 1, THAC or TDAC 1, and THDE or TDDE 1 recommended.

courses.subject: TDDR
courses.title: Text Analysis for Actors and Directors
courses.description: An introduction to analyzing text from a director’s point of view as part of a director’s preproduction process. The class will focus on analyzing story, the underlying dramatic structure in terms of dramatic action, narrative vision, and artistic drive.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor. Restricted to students within the TH26 major. All other students will be allowed as space permits.

courses.subject: TDDR
courses.title: Major Project in Directing
courses.description: For the advanced student in directing. Intensive concentration on the full realization of a dramatic text from research and analysis through rehearsal and into performance. A maximum of eight units of major project study, regardless of area (design, directing, or stage management) may be used to fulfill major requirements. See department for application. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: TDDR 108, TDDR 111, consent of instructor, and department stamp.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Introduction to Theatre
courses.description: An introduction to fundamental concepts in drama and performance. Students will attend performances and learn about how the theatre functions as an art and as an industry in today’s world.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Theatre and Film
courses.description: Theatre and Film analyzes the essential differences between theatrical and cinematic approaches to drama. Through selected play/film combinations, the course looks at how the director uses actors and the visual languages of the stage and screen to guide and stimulate the audience’s responses.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Great Performances on Film
courses.description: Course examines major accomplishments in screen acting from the work of actors in films or in film genres. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Public Speaking
courses.description: This course is designed to establish a clear understanding of the fundamentals of effective oral communication. The methodologies explore the integration of relaxation, concentration, organization, and clear voice and diction as applied to various public speaking modes.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Dance and Social Movement(s)
courses.description: This course studies movement practices from social dancing to political protest, including embodiments framed explicitly as dance as well as those not readily legible as such. How is moving a form of citizenry, refusal, community-building, art-making, remembrance, and communal forgetting? Framed as knowledge-making systems, students will attend to how dance and movement varyingly articulate belonging, joy, and discipline in relation to histories of race, gender, sexuality, ability, class, and nation.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Cult Films: Weirdly Dramatic
courses.description: A select survey of eight to ten exceptional offbeat, frequently low-budget films from the last sixty years that have attained cult status. The mix includes Tod Browning’s Freaks (1932) to John Water’s Pink Flamingos (1973). Aspects of bad taste, cinematic irony, and theatrical invention will be highlighted.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Topics in Theatre and Film
courses.description: Great films and the performance of the actors in them are analyzed in their historical, cinematic, or theatrical contexts. This course examines the actor’s contribution to classic cinema and the social and aesthetic forces at work in film. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGE
courses.title: Special Projects
courses.description: Qualified students will pursue a special project in theatre history, problems of production and performance, and similarly appropriate topics.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, 2.5 GPA, consent of instructor, and department stamp.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Acting Practicum
courses.description: One-on-one laboratory workshop that examines practical applications of accents, speech and voice work, dialect, movement and combat work specific and ancillary to the productions in which the students have been cast.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Directing Process Studio
courses.description: Preparation, presentation, and discussion of representative scenes from various periods of dramatic literature.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Process II: Classical Text I
courses.description: An intensive studio examination of problems and potentials associated with the theatrical realization of the classical text.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Speech for the Actor II
courses.description: Advanced work in phonetics and articulation. Intensive study of stage dialects to prepare actor for variety of roles.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing; THGR or TDGR 221A prerequisite for THGR or TDGR 221B; admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Movement for Theatre II
courses.description: An advanced course in the art of movement for the theatre, building on the knowledge gained in Theatre 213. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: THGR or TDGR 223A for B; admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Voice for Theatre II
courses.description: Advanced voice training designed to help the actor fuse voice, emotion, and body into a fully realized reflection of the text. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: THGR or TDGR 224A for B; admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Singing for the Actor II
courses.description: Continuing vocal technique for the musical theatre. More complicated musical material investigated and prepared.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Theatre Externship
courses.description: Selected professional opportunities in repertory and commercial theatre, designed to engage the student in particular creative responsibilities under the guidance of master artist-teachers. Student is expected to give biweekly reports detailing his/her experience with the professional company.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Skills
courses.description: A unifying approach to acting skills (voice, movement, and speech) designed to result in providing the graduating actor with a daily regimen appropriate for professional work.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Directing Seminar
courses.description: A seminar focusing on the current directing projects of all graduate directing students.
